# bento-shad-ui v0.2.2: full documentation for LLMs

> Every guide and every component page in one file. Source: https://github.com/SaadNiaziDev/bento-shad-ui/tree/main/docs. Website: https://saadniazidev.github.io/bento-shad-ui/. Index: llms.txt.

<!-- docs/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

bento-shad-ui is a UI library for interfaces laid out as bento grids: rounded tiles of different sizes, one idea per tile. The components follow shadcn/ui anatomy and token names, so the library fits next to shadcn and Tailwind, and it also works on a plain HTML page and in Flutter.

## One token file, five ways to use it

Every colour, radius and font lives in `src/tokens.json`. The build turns it into:

| Layer | Import | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| CSS | `bento-shad-ui/bento.css` | Any website or web app. Classes start with `bk-`. |
| Core (TypeScript) | `bento-shad-ui` or the CDN script | You want theme switching, tabs, dialogs, menus, toasts and the command palette to work from HTML attributes. |
| React | `bento-shad-ui/react` | React 18/19, Next.js, Vite. Typed components with no Tailwind needed. |
| shadcn theme + registry | `bento-shad-ui/shadcn-theme.css`, `npx shadcn add …/r/bento-theme.json` | You already use shadcn/ui and Tailwind v4 and want this look plus `BentoGrid`/`BentoTile`. |
| Flutter | `dist/flutter/bento_theme.dart` | Flutter apps: `ThemeData` for light and dark plus every token as a `ThemeExtension`. |

You can mix layers: for example a Next.js marketing site on `bento-shad-ui/react` and a Flutter app on `bento_theme.dart` share the same colours.

## Quick start: plain HTML

```html
<!doctype html>
<html
    lang="en"
    data-theme="system"
>
    <head>
        <meta
            name="viewport"
            content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"
        />
        <link
            rel="stylesheet"
            href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Red+Hat+Display:wght@500;600;700;800&family=Red+Hat+Text:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap"
        />
        <link
            rel="stylesheet"
            href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/bento.min.css"
        />
        <script
            src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/bento.iife.min.js"
            defer
        ></script>
    </head>
    <body class="bk">
        <main class="bk-container">
            <div class="bk-bento">
                <div class="bk-bento-grid">
                    <article
                        class="bk-tile bk-span-2 bk-row-2"
                        data-tone="inverse"
                    >
                        <h1 class="bk-h1">Hello</h1>
                        <button
                            class="bk-button"
                            data-variant="brand"
                            data-bk-toast='{"title":"It works"}'
                        >
                            Try me
                        </button>
                    </article>
                    <article
                        class="bk-tile"
                        data-tone="peach"
                    >
                        One idea
                    </article>
                    <article class="bk-tile">Another idea</article>
                </div>
            </div>
        </main>
    </body>
</html>
```

## Quick start: React / Next.js

```bash
npm install bento-shad-ui
```

```tsx
import 'bento-shad-ui/bento.css';
import { BentoGrid, Tile, TileTitle, Button, toast } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

export default function Page() {
    return (
        <BentoGrid>
            <Tile
                span={2}
                rows={2}
                tone="inverse"
            >
                <TileTitle>Hello</TileTitle>
                <Button
                    variant="brand"
                    onClick={() => toast({ title: 'It works' })}
                >
                    Try me
                </Button>
            </Tile>
            <Tile tone="peach">One idea</Tile>
            <Tile>Another idea</Tile>
        </BentoGrid>
    );
}
```

Add `className="bk"` to `<body>` (or wrap your app in an element with it) so base typography and colours apply.

## Core ideas

- **Tokens** are CSS variables with shadcn's names (`--background`, `--primary`, `--muted-foreground`…) plus bento extras (`--brand`, `--success`, `--inverse`, `--tint-peach`…). Components use nothing else, so changing a token restyles everything.
- **Tiles** are the unit of layout. A tile spans 1–4 columns and 1–3 rows. Grids follow their container's width (container queries), so the same markup works in a sidebar, a modal or a full page.
- **Tones** (`data-tone` / `tone`) colour a tile and adjust the tokens inside it, so buttons and inputs in a peach or inverse tile still look right.
- **Variants** are attributes in HTML (`data-variant="outline"`, `data-size="sm"`) and props in React (`variant="outline" size="sm"`).
- **Dark mode** is `class="dark"` or `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>`; `data-theme="system"` follows the OS.
- **No monospace font.** The library uses Red Hat Display for headings and Red Hat Text for everything else, including code and keyboard keys.

## Versioning

The library follows semantic versioning. Class names, data attributes, token names and React props are the public API. Until 1.0, minor versions (0.x.0) may include breaking changes and say so in `CHANGELOG.md`; patch versions never do. npm ranges like `^0.2.2` only accept patch releases while the version is below 1.0, so updates never surprise you. Pin exact versions in CDN URLs.

# Installation

Requirements: a current browser (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox from 2024 on). For npm installs, Node 18+. For React, React 18 or 19.

## 1. npm

```bash
npm install bento-shad-ui
# pnpm add bento-shad-ui
# yarn add bento-shad-ui
# bun add bento-shad-ui
```

[bento-shad-ui on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bento-shad-ui). Releases are published from GitHub Actions with npm provenance, so each version links to the commit it was built from.

What you can import:

| Import | What it is |
|---|---|
| `bento-shad-ui/bento.css` | Tokens + all component styles (`bento.min.css` for the minified file) |
| `bento-shad-ui/tokens.css` | Tokens only (CSS variables for light and dark) |
| `bento-shad-ui` | Typed vanilla core: `start`, `init`, `toast`, `setTheme`, `themeScript`… (ESM, SSR-safe) |
| `bento-shad-ui/auto` | Same as above, and starts the behaviours on import |
| `bento-shad-ui/react` | React components (ESM, marked `"use client"`) |
| `bento-shad-ui/shadcn-theme.css` | `globals.css` for shadcn/ui on Tailwind v4 |
| `bento-shad-ui/tokens.json` | Raw tokens for other tools |
| `bento-shad-ui/flutter/bento_theme.dart` | Flutter theme (copy it into `lib/`) |
| `bento-shad-ui/llms-full.txt` | All docs in one file for AI agents |

The package is ESM-only. Bundlers (Next.js, Vite, webpack 5, esbuild) handle it with no config.

To install an unreleased commit, or your own fork, install from GitHub instead: `npm install github:SaadNiaziDev/bento-shad-ui#main`.

## 2. CDN (no build step)

jsDelivr and unpkg serve every npm version. Pin the exact version in production:

```html
<link
    rel="stylesheet"
    href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/bento.min.css"
/>
<script
    src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/bento.iife.min.js"
    defer
></script>
```

`https://unpkg.com/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/bento.min.css` works the same way. The script exposes `window.BentoUI` (`BentoUI.toast(...)`, `BentoUI.setTheme('dark')`) and starts itself.

As an ES module without a bundler:

```html
<script type="module">
    import {
        start,
        toast,
    } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/index.js';
    start();
</script>
```

## 3. shadcn/ui registry

In a project that already ran `npx shadcn@latest init`:

```bash
# 1. theme: colours, fonts, radius, tile sizes, light + dark. --overwrite is required
npx shadcn@latest add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SaadNiaziDev/bento-shad-ui/v0.2.2/r/bento-theme.json --overwrite
# 2. BentoGrid + BentoTile component and the bento-grid / bento-tile utilities
npx shadcn@latest add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SaadNiaziDev/bento-shad-ui/v0.2.2/r/bento-grid.json
```

Without `--overwrite`, shadcn only adds the new tokens (`--brand`, `--tint-*`…) and keeps its own values for existing ones (`--primary`, `--radius`, `--font-sans`), leaving you with half of each theme.

Or copy `dist/shadcn-theme.css` over `app/globals.css`. See [shadcn.md](shadcn.md).

## 4. Flutter

Copy `dist/flutter/bento_theme.dart` into `lib/` (from `node_modules/bento-shad-ui/dist/flutter/` or from the CDN):

```bash
curl -o lib/bento_theme.dart https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/flutter/bento_theme.dart
```

See [flutter.md](flutter.md).

## Fonts

The library expects **Red Hat Display** (headings) and **Red Hat Text** (body). Both are free under the SIL Open Font License. There is no monospace font.

Google Fonts:

```html
<link
    rel="preconnect"
    href="https://fonts.googleapis.com"
/>
<link
    rel="preconnect"
    href="https://fonts.gstatic.com"
    crossorigin
/>
<link
    rel="stylesheet"
    href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Red+Hat+Display:wght@500;600;700;800&family=Red+Hat+Text:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap"
/>
```

Next.js (`next/font`, self-hosted, no layout shift):

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { Red_Hat_Display, Red_Hat_Text } from 'next/font/google';
const text = Red_Hat_Text({ subsets: ['latin'], variable: '--font-rh-text' });
const display = Red_Hat_Display({
    subsets: ['latin'],
    variable: '--font-rh-display',
});
// <html className={`${text.variable} ${display.variable}`}> …
```

```css
/* globals.css, after bento.css */
:root {
    --font-sans: var(--font-rh-text), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
    --font-heading:
        var(--font-rh-display), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

If the fonts fail to load, the system UI font is used; nothing breaks.

## Updating

```bash
npm install bento-shad-ui@latest
npm outdated bento-shad-ui   # what you have vs. the newest version
```

Read the [changelog](https://github.com/SaadNiaziDev/bento-shad-ui/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) first: until 1.0, a minor version (0.x.0) can contain breaking changes. For CDN links, change the version in the URL.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Components have no styles | Import `bento-shad-ui/bento.css` once, and add `class="bk"` to `<body>`. |
| `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` | The package is ESM-only. Use `import`, or set `"type": "module"`. |
| Dark mode flashes on load | Add the theme script to `<head>`: `<ThemeScript />` in React, `themeScript` string elsewhere. See [theming.md](theming.md). |
| Menus or popovers don't open | They use the native `popover` attribute (browsers since 2024). Update the browser. |
| Next.js: "functions cannot be passed to Client Components" | Event-handler props (`onClick`, `onValueChange`) need a component marked `"use client"`. |
| Grid stays at one column | `.bk-bento-grid` must sit inside `.bk-bento` (React's `BentoGrid` does this for you). |

<!-- docs/examples.md -->

# Examples

> Build a dashboard, workspace settings, pricing page and onboarding flow with copyable component compositions.

These examples combine the same components used throughout the kit. Switch the site theme to see each composition in light and dark mode, then open the HTML tab to copy it. The data is illustrative. Buttons that show toasts demonstrate local feedback; connect persistence, authentication and billing in your application.

## Analytics overview

Use a wide tile for the main story and smaller tiles for supporting metrics. Give charts a text alternative and keep the scale consistent. Built with [Bento grid](components/bento-grid.md), [Stat](components/stat.md), [Bar chart](components/bar-chart.md) and [Table](components/table.md).

```html
<div class="bk-bento">
    <div class="bk-bento-grid">
        <article class="bk-tile bk-span-2">
            <div class="bk-stat">
                <span class="bk-stat-label">Monthly revenue</span>
                <span class="bk-stat-value">$24,680</span>
                <span
                    class="bk-stat-delta"
                    data-trend="up"
                >
                    +18.6% from last month
                </span>
            </div>
        </article>
        <article class="bk-tile bk-span-2">
            <div class="bk-stat">
                <span class="bk-stat-label">Active subscriptions</span>
                <span class="bk-stat-value">1,482</span>
                <span
                    class="bk-stat-delta"
                    data-trend="up"
                >
                    +124 from last month
                </span>
            </div>
        </article>
        <article class="bk-tile bk-span-full">
            <div class="bk-tile-header">
                <div>
                    <h3 class="bk-tile-title">Revenue, in perspective</h3>
                    <p class="bk-tile-description">
                        Last six months · USD thousands · scale 0–30
                    </p>
                </div>
                <span
                    class="bk-badge"
                    data-variant="outline"
                >
                    Monthly
                </span>
            </div>
            <div
                class="bk-chart"
                role="img"
                aria-label="Revenue: June $12,000; July $18,000; August $15,000; September $21,000; October $24,000; November $24,680."
            >
                <div class="bk-bars">
                    <div
                        class="bk-bar"
                        data-muted
                        style="--v: 40%"
                        data-value="$12k"
                    ></div>
                    <div
                        class="bk-bar"
                        data-muted
                        style="--v: 60%"
                        data-value="$18k"
                    ></div>
                    <div
                        class="bk-bar"
                        data-muted
                        style="--v: 50%"
                        data-value="$15k"
                    ></div>
                    <div
                        class="bk-bar"
                        data-muted
                        style="--v: 70%"
                        data-value="$21k"
                    ></div>
                    <div
                        class="bk-bar"
                        data-muted
                        style="--v: 80%"
                        data-value="$24k"
                    ></div>
                    <div
                        class="bk-bar"
                        style="--v: 82.27%"
                        data-value="$24.68k"
                    ></div>
                </div>
                <div class="bk-bar-labels">
                    <span>Jun</span>
                    <span>Jul</span>
                    <span>Aug</span>
                    <span>Sep</span>
                    <span>Oct</span>
                    <span>Nov</span>
                </div>
            </div>
        </article>
        <article class="bk-tile bk-span-full">
            <h3 class="bk-tile-title">Recent invoices</h3>
            <div class="bk-table-wrap">
                <table class="bk-table">
                    <caption>
                        Illustrative customer invoices for November
                    </caption>
                    <thead>
                        <tr>
                            <th scope="col">Customer</th>
                            <th scope="col">Status</th>
                            <th
                                scope="col"
                                data-align="end"
                            >
                                Amount
                            </th>
                        </tr>
                    </thead>
                    <tbody>
                        <tr>
                            <td>Studio North</td>
                            <td>
                                <span
                                    class="bk-badge"
                                    data-variant="success"
                                >
                                    Paid
                                </span>
                            </td>
                            <td data-align="end">$240.00</td>
                        </tr>
                        <tr>
                            <td>Forma Design</td>
                            <td>
                                <span
                                    class="bk-badge"
                                    data-variant="warning"
                                >
                                    Pending
                                </span>
                            </td>
                            <td data-align="end">$120.00</td>
                        </tr>
                        <tr>
                            <td>Orbit Labs</td>
                            <td>
                                <span
                                    class="bk-badge"
                                    data-variant="outline"
                                >
                                    Draft
                                </span>
                            </td>
                            <td data-align="end">$480.00</td>
                        </tr>
                    </tbody>
                </table>
            </div>
        </article>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Workspace settings

Use visible labels, helpful descriptions and native controls. This preview uses a button to demonstrate feedback; a real form should validate and save before reporting success. Built with [Field](components/field.md), [Input](components/input.md), [Switch](components/switch.md) and [Card](components/card.md).

```html
<section
    class="bk-card"
    aria-labelledby="example-settings-title"
>
    <div class="bk-card-header">
        <h3
            class="bk-card-title"
            id="example-settings-title"
        >
            Workspace settings
        </h3>
        <p class="bk-card-description">The details your team sees.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-content bk-form">
        <div class="bk-form-row">
            <div class="bk-field">
                <label
                    class="bk-label"
                    for="example-workspace"
                >
                    Workspace name
                </label>
                <input
                    class="bk-input"
                    id="example-workspace"
                    value="Studio North"
                    autocomplete="organization"
                />
            </div>
            <div class="bk-field">
                <label
                    class="bk-label"
                    for="example-email"
                >
                    Contact email
                </label>
                <input
                    class="bk-input"
                    type="email"
                    id="example-email"
                    value="hello@example.com"
                    autocomplete="email"
                />
            </div>
        </div>
        <div class="bk-field">
            <label
                class="bk-label"
                for="example-timezone"
            >
                Time zone
            </label>
            <select
                class="bk-select"
                id="example-timezone"
            >
                <option>Asia/Karachi (UTC+05:00)</option>
                <option>Europe/London</option>
                <option>America/New_York</option>
            </select>
        </div>
        <hr class="bk-separator" />
        <label class="bk-switch-row">
            <span class="bk-option-text">
                <span>Weekly digest</span>
                <span>A summary of activity in your workspace.</span>
            </span>
            <input
                class="bk-switch"
                type="checkbox"
                role="switch"
                checked
            />
        </label>
        <label class="bk-switch-row">
            <span class="bk-option-text">
                <span>Product updates</span>
                <span>Occasional news about new features.</span>
            </span>
            <input
                class="bk-switch"
                type="checkbox"
                role="switch"
            />
        </label>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-footer">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            type="button"
            data-bk-toast='{"title":"Preview only","description":"Connect this form to your save handler.","variant":"info"}'
        >
            Preview save feedback
        </button>
    </div>
</section>
```

## Subscription plans

A neutral comparison keeps the recommended plan in focus. Prices are example content; these controls do not start checkout. Built with [Card](components/card.md), [Badge](components/badge.md) and [Button](components/button.md).

```html
<div class="bk-bento">
    <div class="bk-bento-grid">
        <article class="bk-tile bk-span-2">
            <span class="bk-eyebrow">Personal</span>
            <h3 class="bk-tile-title">Space to explore</h3>
            <div class="bk-stat">
                <span class="bk-stat-value">$0</span>
                <span class="bk-stat-label">Free, for personal projects</span>
            </div>
            <ul>
                <li>3 projects</li>
                <li>Community support</li>
                <li>Core components</li>
            </ul>
            <button
                class="bk-button"
                data-variant="outline"
                type="button"
                data-bk-toast='{"title":"Personal plan preview","description":"Add your sign-up flow here."}'
            >
                Start a project
            </button>
        </article>
        <article
            class="bk-tile bk-span-2"
            data-tone="mint"
        >
            <div class="bk-row bk-between">
                <span class="bk-eyebrow">Team</span>
                <span
                    class="bk-badge"
                    data-variant="outline"
                >
                    For growing teams
                </span>
            </div>
            <h3 class="bk-tile-title">Build together</h3>
            <div class="bk-stat">
                <span class="bk-stat-value">$24</span>
                <span class="bk-stat-label">
                    Per member / month, billed monthly
                </span>
            </div>
            <ul>
                <li>Unlimited projects</li>
                <li>Shared workspaces</li>
                <li>Priority support</li>
            </ul>
            <button
                class="bk-button"
                data-variant="brand"
                type="button"
                data-bk-toast='{"title":"Team plan preview","description":"Connect your billing provider to start checkout."}'
            >
                Explore Team
            </button>
        </article>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Onboarding checklist

Use native checkboxes for tasks and keep the action close to its context. This example lets people check tasks locally; it does not persist progress. Built with [Checkbox](components/checkbox.md), [Alert](components/alert.md) and [Button](components/button.md).

```html
<section
    class="bk-card"
    aria-labelledby="example-onboarding-title"
>
    <div class="bk-card-header">
        <span class="bk-eyebrow">Your first workspace</span>
        <h3
            class="bk-card-title"
            id="example-onboarding-title"
        >
            Make yourself at home
        </h3>
        <p class="bk-card-description">
            A few small steps to get your team moving.
        </p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-content bk-stack">
        <label class="bk-option">
            <input
                class="bk-checkbox"
                type="checkbox"
                checked
            />
            <span class="bk-option-text">
                <span>Name your workspace</span>
                <span>Pick something your team will recognise.</span>
            </span>
        </label>
        <label class="bk-option">
            <input
                class="bk-checkbox"
                type="checkbox"
            />
            <span class="bk-option-text">
                <span>Create your first project</span>
                <span>Start with one goal and a few tasks.</span>
            </span>
        </label>
        <label class="bk-option">
            <input
                class="bk-checkbox"
                type="checkbox"
            />
            <span class="bk-option-text">
                <span>Invite a teammate</span>
                <span>Good work is better together.</span>
            </span>
        </label>
        <div
            class="bk-alert"
            role="note"
        >
            <div>
                <div class="bk-alert-title">Go at your own pace</div>
                <p class="bk-alert-description">
                    You can return to this checklist whenever you like.
                </p>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-footer">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            type="button"
            data-bk-toast='{"title":"Invitation preview","description":"Connect your invitation handler here."}'
        >
            Preview invitation
        </button>
    </div>
</section>
```

## Use these patterns in React

Import the stylesheet once. React components use props in place of HTML data attributes; use application state for data and event handlers for actions. See the [React guide](react.md) for setup and the component pages for the full prop tables.

```tsx
import 'bento-shad-ui/bento.css';
import { BentoGrid, Tile, Stat, Button, toast } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

export function Overview() {
    return (
        <BentoGrid>
            <Tile>
                <Stat
                    label="Monthly revenue"
                    value="$24,680"
                    delta="+18.6%"
                    trend="up"
                />
            </Tile>
            <Tile>
                <Stat
                    label="Active projects"
                    value="12"
                />
            </Tile>
            <Tile span={2}>
                <Button onClick={() => toast({ title: 'Preview only' })}>
                    Preview feedback
                </Button>
            </Tile>
        </BentoGrid>
    );
}
```

<!-- docs/html.md -->

# Using with plain HTML

Works with any server or static site: plain HTML, PHP, Rails, Django, Laravel, htmx, Astro, Eleventy.

## Page setup

```html
<!doctype html>
<html
    lang="en"
    data-theme="system"
>
    <head>
        <meta charset="utf-8" />
        <meta
            name="viewport"
            content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"
        />
        <!-- 1. no dark-mode flash: copy the string exported as `themeScript`, or this line -->
        <script>
            (function () {
                try {
                    var r = document.documentElement,
                        t = null;
                    try {
                        t = localStorage.getItem('bk-theme');
                    } catch (e) {}
                    if (t !== 'light' && t !== 'dark' && t !== 'system')
                        t = r.getAttribute('data-theme') || 'system';
                    var d =
                        t === 'dark' ||
                        (t === 'system' &&
                            window.matchMedia &&
                            matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches);
                    r.setAttribute('data-theme', t);
                    r.classList.toggle('dark', d);
                } catch (e) {}
            })();
        </script>
        <!-- 2. fonts -->
        <link
            rel="stylesheet"
            href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Red+Hat+Display:wght@500;600;700;800&family=Red+Hat+Text:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap"
        />
        <!-- 3. styles and behaviours -->
        <link
            rel="stylesheet"
            href="/vendor/bento-shad-ui/bento.min.css"
        />
        <script
            src="/vendor/bento-shad-ui/bento.iife.min.js"
            defer
        ></script>
    </head>
    <body class="bk">
        …
    </body>
</html>
```

`class="bk"` on `<body>` sets the font, base size, colours and focus rings. Without it, components still render, but plain text around them uses browser defaults.

## Layout

```html
<main class="bk-container">
    <div class="bk-bento">
        <!-- the box the grid measures -->
        <div class="bk-bento-grid">
            <!-- 4 / 2 / 1 columns -->
            <article class="bk-tile bk-span-2 bk-row-2">…</article>
            <article
                class="bk-tile"
                data-tone="peach"
            >
                …
            </article>
            <article class="bk-tile">…</article>
            <article class="bk-tile bk-span-2">…</article>
        </div>
    </div>
</main>
```

See [layout.md](layout.md) for spans, rows, tones and rules.

## Components

Every component is markup plus classes. Variants are data attributes:

```html
<button
    class="bk-button"
    data-variant="outline"
    data-size="sm"
>
    Share
</button>
<span
    class="bk-badge"
    data-variant="success"
    data-dot
>
    Paid
</span>
<div
    class="bk-alert"
    data-variant="destructive"
    role="alert"
>
    …
</div>
```

The full catalogue with markup is in [components.md](components.md). The live kit (`index.html`) has a **Code** button on every tile.

## Behaviours (optional script)

Without JavaScript, everything renders and these still work: buttons, inputs, native selects, checkboxes, radios, switches, sliders, accordions (`<details>`) and tooltips (CSS). The script adds the following, driven by attributes:

| Attribute / class | What happens |
|---|---|
| `data-bk-theme-set="light\|dark\|system"` | Click sets the theme and remembers it |
| `data-bk-open="id"` on a button | Opens `<dialog id="id">` (dialog, sheet, command) |
| `data-bk-close` inside a dialog | Closes it. `data-bk-close="value"` sets `returnValue` |
| `popovertarget="id"` + `.bk-menu[popover]` / `.bk-popover[popover]` | Places the menu under its button and flips it when there's no room |
| `data-bk-toast='{"title":"Saved","variant":"success"}'` | Shows a toast on click |
| `data-bk-copy="text"` or `data-bk-copy-target="#selector"` | Copies to the clipboard and confirms with a toast |
| `[data-bk-tabs]` with `role="tab"` + `aria-controls` | Tabs with arrow-key navigation |
| `.bk-toggle` (in `.bk-toggle-group[data-type="single"]` for one-of) | Flips `aria-pressed` |
| `.bk-slider` + `<output for="id">` | Keeps the fill and the readout in sync (`data-prefix`, `data-suffix`) |
| `.bk-otp` | Digits only, auto-advance, backspace, paste |
| `.bk-calendar[data-mode="single\|range"]` | Day selection; fires `bk:change` with `{ start, end }` |
| `dialog.bk-command[data-bk-hotkey]` | ⌘K / Ctrl+K opens it; typing filters `.bk-command-item`s |
| `.bk-dropzone` | Drag-over state and selected file names |

Content added later (fetch, htmx swaps, Turbo) is set up automatically through a `MutationObserver`. To control it yourself, load the ES module and call `start({ observe: false })`, then `init(newElement)` after each swap.

### Calling it from your own code

```js
BentoUI.toast({
    title: 'Trip saved',
    description: 'Lisbon, 12–16 March',
    variant: 'success',
});
BentoUI.setTheme('dark');
document.addEventListener('bk:theme', (e) => console.log(e.detail)); // { theme, resolved }
```

Full API: [javascript-api.md](javascript-api.md).

## Self-hosting the files

Copy from `node_modules/bento-shad-ui/dist/` (or the GitHub release) into your static folder:

- `bento.min.css` (and `bento.css` for readable source)
- `bento.iife.min.js`

There are no other assets: icons are inline SVG you provide, and fonts come from Google Fonts or your own copy.

## Icons

The kit doesn't ship an icon set. Any 24×24 stroke icon works; Lucide matches best. Give inline SVGs `class="bk-icon"` (16px, `data-size="sm|lg|xl"` for 14/20/24px). SVGs placed directly inside buttons, menu items, sidebar items and similar are sized automatically.

<!-- docs/react.md -->

# Using with React and Next.js

`bento-shad-ui/react` is a set of typed React components that render the kit's classes. It needs no Tailwind. The bundle starts with `"use client"`, works with React 18 and 19, and renders on the server (no `window` access at import time).

## Install

```bash
npm install bento-shad-ui
```

## Next.js App Router

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import 'bento-shad-ui/bento.css';
import './globals.css'; // your overrides, after the kit
import { Red_Hat_Display, Red_Hat_Text } from 'next/font/google';
import { ThemeScript } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

const text = Red_Hat_Text({ subsets: ['latin'], variable: '--font-rh-text' });
const display = Red_Hat_Display({
    subsets: ['latin'],
    variable: '--font-rh-display',
});

export default function RootLayout({
    children,
}: {
    children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
    return (
        <html
            lang="en"
            data-theme="system"
            className={`${text.variable} ${display.variable}`}
            suppressHydrationWarning
        >
            <head>
                <ThemeScript />
            </head>
            <body className="bk">{children}</body>
        </html>
    );
}
```

```css
/* app/globals.css */
:root {
    --font-sans: var(--font-rh-text), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
    --font-heading:
        var(--font-rh-display), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

- `ThemeScript` applies the saved theme before the first paint, so dark mode doesn't flash.
- `suppressHydrationWarning` is needed because that script changes `<html>` attributes before React hydrates.
- Server components can render kit components. Event-handler props (`onClick`, `onValueChange`, `onOpenChange`) must come from a component marked `"use client"`, as with any React library.

## Vite / Create React App

```tsx
// main.tsx
import 'bento-shad-ui/bento.css';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App';
document.body.classList.add('bk');
createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);
```

## A page

```tsx
'use client';
import { useState } from 'react';
import {
    BentoGrid,
    Tile,
    TileHeader,
    TileTitle,
    TileDescription,
    Eyebrow,
    Button,
    Badge,
    Stat,
    Sparkline,
    BarChart,
    Field,
    Input,
    Switch,
    Dialog,
    toast,
} from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

export function Dashboard() {
    const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
    return (
        <BentoGrid>
            <Tile
                span={2}
                rows={2}
                tone="inverse"
            >
                <Eyebrow>This week</Eyebrow>
                <BarChart
                    data={[
                        { label: 'Mon', value: 32 },
                        { label: 'Tue', value: 45 },
                        { label: 'Wed', value: 28 },
                    ]}
                    formatValue={(v) => `${v} bookings`}
                />
            </Tile>
            <Tile>
                <Stat
                    label="Revenue"
                    value="€48,210"
                    delta="+8.1% vs February"
                    trend="up"
                />
                <Sparkline
                    data={[12, 18, 15, 22, 19, 27, 31]}
                    label="Revenue rose all week"
                />
            </Tile>
            <Tile tone="peach">
                <TileHeader>
                    <div>
                        <TileTitle>Price alerts</TileTitle>
                        <TileDescription>
                            We tell you when fares drop.
                        </TileDescription>
                    </div>
                    <Badge variant="brand">New</Badge>
                </TileHeader>
                <Switch
                    label="Email me"
                    defaultChecked
                />
            </Tile>
            <Tile>
                <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Edit profile</Button>
                <Dialog
                    open={open}
                    onOpenChange={setOpen}
                    title="Edit profile"
                    description="Your name shows on shared trips."
                    footer={
                        <>
                            <Button
                                variant="outline"
                                onClick={() => setOpen(false)}
                            >
                                Cancel
                            </Button>
                            <Button
                                onClick={() => {
                                    setOpen(false);
                                    toast({
                                        title: 'Saved',
                                        variant: 'success',
                                    });
                                }}
                            >
                                Save
                            </Button>
                        </>
                    }
                >
                    <Field label="Name">
                        <Input defaultValue="Maya Kim" />
                    </Field>
                </Dialog>
            </Tile>
        </BentoGrid>
    );
}
```

## Patterns

**Router links.** Every link-like component takes `asChild`:

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link';

<Button asChild>
    <Link href="/trips">Trips</Link>
</Button>
<NavbarLink asChild current>
    <Link href="/">Home</Link>
</NavbarLink>
<SidebarItem asChild icon={<Home />}>
    <Link href="/">Home</Link>
</SidebarItem>
<Tile asChild interactive>
    <Link href="/trips/lisbon">…</Link>
</Tile>
```

**Forms.** `Field` creates the id and wires `htmlFor`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`:

```tsx
<Field
    label="Email"
    description="We'll send the itinerary here."
    error={errors.email}
    required
>
    <Input
        type="email"
        name="email"
    />
</Field>;
```

It works with react-hook-form (`<Input {...register('email')} />`) and with server actions (plain `name` attributes).

**Controlled or uncontrolled.** Stateful components accept both: `value` + `onValueChange`, or `defaultValue`. The same goes for `pressed`, `checked`, `open` and `month`.

**Toasts.** `toast()` works from anywhere, with no provider:

```tsx
toast({
    title: 'Payment failed',
    description: 'Your card was declined.',
    variant: 'destructive',
    action: { label: 'Retry', onClick: retry },
});
```

**Theme.**

```tsx
const { theme, resolvedTheme, setTheme } = useTheme();
<ThemeToggle />; // Light / Dark / System
```

**Command palette.**

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); // ⌘K / Ctrl+K toggles it
<CommandDialog
    open={open}
    onOpenChange={setOpen}
    groups={[
        {
            heading: 'Pages',
            items: [
                {
                    id: 'trips',
                    label: 'Trips',
                    onSelect: () => router.push('/trips'),
                },
            ],
        },
    ]}
/>;
```

## Icons

Pass any React icon as children or as an `icon` prop. lucide-react matches the kit:

```tsx
import { Plus } from 'lucide-react';
<Button>
    <Plus />
    Add trip
</Button>;
```

SVGs inside buttons, menu items, sidebar items, badges and similar are sized to 16px automatically (20px in the bottom nav).

## Using it with the vanilla core

You don't need `bento-shad-ui` (the core) in a React app. If a page also contains plain-HTML kit markup and you call `start()`, the core leaves React-rendered components alone: they carry `data-bk-react`.

Every component and prop is listed in [components.md](components.md).

<!-- docs/shadcn.md -->

# Using with shadcn/ui and Tailwind v4

If a project already uses shadcn/ui, keep its components and add the bento theme and grid. You get shadcn components in this colour system, the Red Hat fonts and the `BentoGrid` / `BentoTile` layout.

## Option A: registry (recommended)

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SaadNiaziDev/bento-shad-ui/v0.2.2/r/bento-theme.json --overwrite
npx shadcn@latest add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SaadNiaziDev/bento-shad-ui/v0.2.2/r/bento-grid.json
```

- `bento-theme` writes the tokens into your CSS file (`:root`, `.dark`, `@theme inline`): every shadcn colour, the radius, the Red Hat fonts, and new tokens such as `--color-brand` and `--color-tint-peach` so `bg-brand` or `text-tint-sky-foreground` work. **Use `--overwrite`.** Without it, shadcn keeps its own values for tokens that already exist (`--primary`, `--radius`, `--font-sans`) and only adds the new ones.
- `bento-grid` adds `components/ui/bento-grid.tsx`, the `bento-grid` and `bento-tile` utilities and the `class-variance-authority` dependency.

Both commands were tested on a fresh Next.js 15 + Tailwind v4 app, followed by a production build.

## Option B: theme file

Replace `app/globals.css` (or your Tailwind entry CSS) with `node_modules/bento-shad-ui/dist/shadcn-theme.css`, or copy its `@theme inline`, `:root`, `.dark`, `@layer base` and `@utility` blocks into your file. It needs `tailwindcss` v4 and `tw-animate-css` (both installed by `shadcn init`).

## Fonts

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { Red_Hat_Display, Red_Hat_Text } from 'next/font/google';
const text = Red_Hat_Text({ subsets: ['latin'], variable: '--font-rh-text' });
const display = Red_Hat_Display({
    subsets: ['latin'],
    variable: '--font-rh-display',
});
// <html className={`${text.variable} ${display.variable}`}>
```

The theme sets `--font-sans` and `--font-heading` to the Red Hat family names, which works with a Google Fonts `<link>`. With `next/font`, point them at its variables instead:

```css
/* in globals.css, inside @theme inline: point the font tokens at next/font */
@theme inline {
    --font-sans: var(--font-rh-text), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
    --font-heading:
        var(--font-rh-display), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

Headings (`h1`–`h4`) use `--font-heading` through the base layer. Use `font-heading` on anything else.

## BentoGrid and BentoTile

```tsx
import {
    BentoGrid,
    BentoTile,
    BentoTileHeader,
    BentoTileTitle,
    BentoTileDescription,
} from '@/components/ui/bento-grid';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Switch } from '@/components/ui/switch';

export function Features() {
    return (
        <BentoGrid>
            <BentoTile
                span={2}
                rows={2}
                className="dark bg-background text-foreground border-transparent"
            >
                <BentoTileTitle className="text-2xl">
                    Plan together
                </BentoTileTitle>
                <Button>Invite people</Button>
            </BentoTile>
            <BentoTile tone="peach">
                <BentoTileTitle>Offline maps</BentoTileTitle>
                <BentoTileDescription>
                    Download a city before you fly.
                </BentoTileDescription>
            </BentoTile>
            <BentoTile tone="sky">
                <BentoTileHeader>
                    <BentoTileTitle>Price alerts</BentoTileTitle>
                    <Switch defaultChecked />
                </BentoTileHeader>
            </BentoTile>
            <BentoTile span={2}>…</BentoTile>
        </BentoGrid>
    );
}
```

| Prop | Values | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `span` | `1` `2` `3` `4` `"full"` | Columns from the 2-column breakpoint (`@xl`) up |
| `rows` | `1` `2` `3` | Rows from `@xl` up |
| `tone` | `default` `muted` `peach` `sky` `mint` `lilac` `butter` `inverse` `brand` | Background + text colour |
| `interactive` | `true` | Lift on hover, for clickable tiles |

Breakpoints come from the grid's own width: 1 column, then 2 from `@xl` (36rem), then 4 from `@4xl` (56rem).

**Dark island.** The `inverse` and `brand` tones only change the tile's own colours. shadcn components inside keep the page's tokens. To make a tile, and every component in it, use dark tokens, add the `dark` class: `className="dark bg-background text-foreground"`. Because of `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))`, everything inside switches.

## Using `bento-shad-ui/react` as well

You can, but you rarely need to: shadcn already covers most components. Useful additions from the React package that shadcn lacks: `Stat`, `Sparkline`, `BarChart`, `Meter`, `Ring`, `Empty`, `BottomNav`, `ChoiceCard`, `InputOTP`. If you import them, also import `bento-shad-ui/bento.css`. The tokens are identical, so both sets match.

<!-- docs/flutter.md -->

# Using with Flutter

`dist/flutter/bento_theme.dart` is generated from the same tokens as the CSS. It gives you:

- `BentoTheme.light()` and `BentoTheme.dark()`: Material 3 `ThemeData` with the colour scheme, pill-shaped buttons, outlined inputs and the heading font on display, headline and title styles.
- `BentoColors`: all 49 tokens as a `ThemeExtension`, so every colour (including tints, `brand`, `success`, `inverse`) is available in widgets and animates between light and dark.
- `BentoTheme.tile(...)`: the tile `BoxDecoration`, plus `tileRadius`, `tileGap` and `tilePadding` constants.

It passes `flutter analyze` with no warnings.

## Install

```bash
curl -o lib/theme/bento_theme.dart https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/flutter/bento_theme.dart
```

## Fonts

**Option A, bundled (works offline, recommended for apps).** Download Red Hat Text and Red Hat Display from Google Fonts into `assets/fonts/`, then:

```yaml
# pubspec.yaml
flutter:
  fonts:
    - family: Red Hat Text
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/RedHatText-Regular.ttf
        - asset: assets/fonts/RedHatText-Medium.ttf
          weight: 500
        - asset: assets/fonts/RedHatText-SemiBold.ttf
          weight: 600
        - asset: assets/fonts/RedHatText-Bold.ttf
          weight: 700
    - family: Red Hat Display
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/RedHatDisplay-Bold.ttf
          weight: 700
        - asset: assets/fonts/RedHatDisplay-ExtraBold.ttf
          weight: 800
```

The family names match `BentoTheme.fontFamily` and `BentoTheme.headingFontFamily`, so nothing else is needed.

**Option B, google_fonts package.**

```dart
ThemeData withFonts(ThemeData base) {
  final body = GoogleFonts.redHatTextTextTheme(base.textTheme);
  TextStyle? h(TextStyle? s) => GoogleFonts.redHatDisplay(textStyle: s, fontWeight: FontWeight.w700);
  return base.copyWith(
    textTheme: body.copyWith(
      displayLarge: h(body.displayLarge), displayMedium: h(body.displayMedium), displaySmall: h(body.displaySmall),
      headlineLarge: h(body.headlineLarge), headlineMedium: h(body.headlineMedium), headlineSmall: h(body.headlineSmall),
      titleLarge: h(body.titleLarge),
    ),
  );
}

MaterialApp(theme: withFonts(BentoTheme.light()), darkTheme: withFonts(BentoTheme.dark()));
```

## Use

```dart
import 'theme/bento_theme.dart';

MaterialApp(
  theme: BentoTheme.light(),
  darkTheme: BentoTheme.dark(),
  themeMode: ThemeMode.system,
  home: const HomePage(),
);
```

A bento grid with two columns on phones:

```dart
class BentoTile extends StatelessWidget {
  const BentoTile({super.key, required this.child, this.tint, this.onTint});
  final Widget child;
  final Color? tint;
  final Color? onTint;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final c = Theme.of(context).extension<BentoColors>()!;
    return Container(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.all(BentoTheme.tilePadding),
      decoration: BentoTheme.tile(c, color: tint),
      child: DefaultTextStyle.merge(style: TextStyle(color: onTint ?? c.cardForeground), child: child),
    );
  }
}

// In a page:
final c = Theme.of(context).extension<BentoColors>()!;
GridView.count(
  crossAxisCount: 2,
  mainAxisSpacing: BentoTheme.tileGap,
  crossAxisSpacing: BentoTheme.tileGap,
  padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
  children: [
    BentoTile(tint: c.tintPeach, onTint: c.tintPeachForeground, child: const Text('Budget')),
    BentoTile(tint: c.tintSky, onTint: c.tintSkyForeground, child: const Text('18° Lisbon')),
  ],
);
```

For tiles that span two columns or two rows, use the `flutter_staggered_grid_view` package's `StaggeredGrid.count` with `StaggeredGridTile.count(crossAxisCellCount: 2, mainAxisCellCount: 1, child: …)`.

## Token names

CSS `--tint-peach-foreground` becomes Dart `tintPeachForeground`. The full list is in [theming.md](theming.md).

<!-- docs/theming.md -->

# Theming

## Tokens

All tokens are CSS custom properties on `:root`, redefined for dark mode. The names match shadcn/ui; the bento extras are marked ★.

### Colour

| Token | Used for |
|---|---|
| `--background` / `--foreground` | Page background and default text |
| `--card` / `--card-foreground` | Tiles and cards |
| `--popover` / `--popover-foreground` | Menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts |
| `--primary` / `--primary-foreground` | Default buttons, checked controls, active nav |
| `--secondary` / `--secondary-foreground` | Secondary buttons and badges |
| `--muted` / `--muted-foreground` | Subtle fills (tab list, skeleton) and secondary text |
| `--accent` / `--accent-foreground` | Hover fills for ghost/outline buttons and menu items |
| `--destructive` / `--destructive-foreground` ★ | Delete buttons and error states. The foreground token is an extra: white on light red fails contrast in dark mode, so dark mode uses dark text |
| `--border` | Tile and divider lines |
| `--input` | Form control borders, at least 3:1 against card and background |
| `--ring` | Focus ring, at least 3:1 against card and background |
| `--chart-1` … `--chart-5` | Data series |
| `--sidebar`, `--sidebar-foreground`, `--sidebar-primary`, `--sidebar-primary-foreground`, `--sidebar-accent`, `--sidebar-accent-foreground`, `--sidebar-border`, `--sidebar-ring` | Sidebar |
| `--brand` / `--brand-foreground` ★ | The one accent colour: brand buttons, highlights, rings |
| `--success`, `--warning`, `--info` ★ | Status text and soft badge/alert fills |
| `--inverse` / `--inverse-foreground` ★ | The contrast tile (dark in light mode, light in dark mode) |
| `--tint-peach`, `--tint-sky`, `--tint-mint`, `--tint-lilac`, `--tint-butter` (+ `-foreground`) ★ | Tile tones |

### Size, type, depth

| Token | Default |
|---|---|
| `--radius` | `0.75rem`; `--radius-sm/md/lg/xl/2xl` are 0.6×, 0.8×, 1×, 1.4×, 1.8× |
| `--radius-pill` | `999px` (buttons, badges, tabs) |
| `--tile-radius` ★ | `1.25rem` |
| `--tile-gap` ★ | `12px` |
| `--tile-pad` ★ | `20px` |
| `--font-sans` | Red Hat Text |
| `--font-heading` ★ | Red Hat Display |
| `--shadow-xs/sm/md/lg` | Shadows; tiles have none, overlays use `lg` |

There is deliberately no `--font-mono`. Code and keyboard keys use the sans font with tabular figures.

## Dark mode

| On `<html>` | Result |
|---|---|
| nothing, or `data-theme="light"` | Light |
| `class="dark"` or `data-theme="dark"` | Dark |
| `data-theme="system"` | Follows the OS, live |

`setTheme('light' | 'dark' | 'system')` (core or React) sets both `data-theme` and the `dark` class, saves the choice in `localStorage` under `bk-theme`, and fires `bk:theme`. To avoid a flash of the wrong theme, put the theme script in `<head>`: `<ThemeScript />` in React, or the `themeScript` string from the core elsewhere.

## Rebrand without forking

Override tokens in your own CSS, loaded after the kit:

```css
:root {
    --brand: oklch(0.62 0.19 255); /* blue */
    --brand-foreground: oklch(0.99 0 0);
    --ring: oklch(0.52 0.19 255);
    --radius: 0.75rem;
    --tile-radius: 1.25rem;
}
.dark,
[data-theme='dark'] {
    --brand: oklch(0.7 0.16 255);
    --brand-foreground: oklch(0.15 0 0);
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
    [data-theme='system'] {
        --brand: oklch(0.7 0.16 255);
        --brand-foreground: oklch(0.15 0 0);
    }
}
```

Keep text pairs at 4.5:1 or more and `--ring` / `--input` at 3:1 or more against `--card` and `--background`.

## Rebrand everywhere (fork)

To change the brand for CSS, shadcn and Flutter at once:

1. Fork the repo and edit `src/tokens.json` (hex values; the build converts them to OKLCH).
2. Run `npm run build`, then `npm test`. The tests fail if a light/dark pair falls below WCAG contrast.
3. Commit, tag (`v0.2.2-yourbrand.1`) and install your fork with `npm install github:<you>/bento-shad-ui#v0.2.2-yourbrand.1`.

## Scoped themes

- **Tones** (`data-tone="peach|sky|mint|lilac|butter|muted|inverse|brand"`) recolour a tile and re-point `--foreground`, `--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--secondary`, `--accent` (and for `inverse`/`brand`, `--primary` and `--card`) inside it, so nested components stay readable.
- **Dark island**: `class="dark"` on any element switches its subtree to dark tokens, e.g. a dark hero on a light page.
- **Inverse surface** outside a tile: `class="bk-surface-inverse"`.

## Fonts

Change fonts by overriding the two variables:

```css
:root {
    --font-sans: 'Your Text Face', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
    --font-heading: 'Your Display Face', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

The defaults were chosen to avoid the faces most AI-generated UIs reach for (Inter, Geist, Plus Jakarta Sans, Space Grotesk, Poppins, DM Sans).

<!-- docs/typography.md -->

# Typography

Two faces from one family: **Red Hat Display** for headings and display text, **Red Hat Text** for everything else. Both are free under the SIL Open Font License. The library has no monospace font, by design: code, numbers and keyboard keys use Red Hat Text with tabular figures.

## Scale

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="--gap: 14px"
>
    <div
        class="bk-display"
        style="font-size: 3rem"
    >
        Plan less, go more
    </div>
    <div class="bk-h1">Four nights in Lisbon</div>
    <div class="bk-h2">Day two: Alfama</div>
    <div class="bk-h3">Getting around</div>
    <div class="bk-h4">Tram 28 timetable</div>
    <p class="bk-lead">Everything for the trip, in one place.</p>
    <p class="bk-p">
        Tram 28 leaves Martim Moniz every 12 minutes. Buy a transit card at the
        kiosk first, because drivers don't sell tickets.
    </p>
    <div class="bk-large">Total €640 for 2 travellers</div>
    <div class="bk-small">Updated 2 hours ago</div>
    <div class="bk-muted">Prices include taxes and fees.</div>
    <div class="bk-eyebrow">Itinerary · Day 2</div>
    <div><code class="bk-code">TP 1351 · 08:40 → 10:05</code></div>
</div>
```

| Class | Size / weight | Font | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bk-display` | 40–68px fluid / 800 | Display | Hero headline, once per page |
| `bk-h1` | 40px / 800 | Display | Page title |
| `bk-h2` | 30px / 700 | Display | Section title |
| `bk-h3` | 24px / 700 | Display | Sub-section, big tile title |
| `bk-h4` | 20px / 600 | Display | Small heading |
| `bk-lead` | 20px / 400, muted | Text | Intro paragraph |
| `bk-p` | 16px / 400, 1.75 line height | Text | Body copy, 68 characters max |
| `bk-large` | 18px / 600 | Text | Emphasised value |
| `bk-small` | 14px / 500 | Text | Labels, short notes |
| `bk-muted` | 14px, muted colour | Text | Secondary text |
| `bk-caption` | 12px, muted colour | Text | Captions, footnotes |
| `bk-eyebrow` | 11px / 700, uppercase, tracked | Text | Label above a title |
| `bk-num` | 32px / 700, tabular | Text | Big numbers |
| `bk-code` | 0.9em / 600, tabular, chip | Text | Inline code |
| `bk-codeblock` | 13px, tabular, block | Text | Preformatted code |

Headings tighten their letter spacing as they grow (−0.015em at h4 to −0.045em at display) and use `text-wrap: balance`, so short titles don't leave a single word on the last line.

## Loading the fonts

See [Installation](installation.md#fonts) for Google Fonts, `next/font` and Flutter. To change faces, override two tokens:

```css
:root {
    --font-sans: 'Your Text Face', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
    --font-heading: 'Your Display Face', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

## Guidelines

- One `bk-display` per page, at most. Most pages start at `bk-h1`.
- Keep body text at 16px and lines under about 70 characters.
- Use `bk-num` and tabular figures wherever numbers line up in columns.
- Don't fake headings with bold body text; screen readers navigate by real `h1`–`h4` elements.

<!-- docs/layout.md -->

# Layout: the bento grid

## Structure

```html
<div class="bk-bento">
    <!-- container: the grid measures this element's width -->
    <div class="bk-bento-grid">
        <!-- the grid -->
        <article class="bk-tile">…</article>
    </div>
</div>
```

React: `<BentoGrid>` renders both elements. shadcn: `<BentoGrid>` from `bento-grid.tsx`, or `<div class="@container"><div class="bento-grid">`.

## Columns

Columns follow the **container's** width (container queries), not the viewport. A grid inside a 400px sidebar behaves like a phone layout even on a desktop.

| Container width | Columns |
|---|---|
| more than 900px | 4 (or `data-cols="3"` / `"6"`) |
| 561–900px | 2 |
| 560px or less | 1. Grids with `data-cols="2"` keep 2 down to 300px, for app home screens |

When columns drop, spans reset so a tile never overflows: `span-3` and `span-4` become full width at 2 columns, and every span becomes 1 at 1 column.

## Spans

| HTML class | React prop | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `bk-span-2`, `bk-span-3`, `bk-span-4` | `span={2|3|4}` | Columns |
| `bk-span-full` | `span="full"` | Full row at every width |
| `bk-row-2`, `bk-row-3` | `rows={2|3}` | Rows |

The grid uses `grid-auto-flow: dense`, so later small tiles fill gaps left by large ones.

## Tones

`data-tone` (`tone` prop): `muted`, `peach`, `sky`, `mint`, `lilac`, `butter`, `inverse`, `brand`. Each tone also adjusts the tokens inside the tile, so a `Button`, `Input` or `Badge` placed in it stays readable.

## Tile anatomy

```html
<article class="bk-tile">
    <header class="bk-tile-header">
        <div>
            <h3 class="bk-tile-title">Bookings</h3>
            <p class="bk-tile-description">This week · 330 total</p>
        </div>
        <span
            class="bk-badge"
            data-variant="secondary"
        >
            Week
        </span>
    </header>
    …content…
    <footer class="bk-tile-footer">…</footer>
    <!-- pinned to the bottom -->
</article>
```

Other tile options: `data-interactive` (lifts on hover, for links), `data-center` (centres content), `.bk-tile-media` (an image that bleeds to the tile's top edges), `.bk-eyebrow` (small uppercase label).

## Rules

1. **One idea per tile.** If a tile needs a second heading, split it.
2. **Size by importance.** The main thing gets 2×2; supporting facts get 1×1.
3. **Fill every row.** At 4 columns, choose spans that add up to 4 per row. Check at 2 columns too.
4. **Tint sparingly.** At most one toned tile in four, and one `inverse` tile per view.
5. **Same padding everywhere.** Change a tile's size, not its padding. Adjust `--tile-pad` for the whole grid if needed.
6. **Flat tiles, floating overlays.** Tiles have borders and no shadow; shadows belong to menus, dialogs and toasts.
7. **Content sets the height.** Don't give tiles fixed heights; use `rows` for tall tiles.

## Layout recipes

**Dashboard (4 columns, 3 rows).**
Sidebar `rows=3` · three stat tiles · chart `span=2` · activity `rows=2` · table `span=2`.

**Landing feature section (8 cells).**
Hero feature `span=2 rows=2 tone=inverse` · two 1×1 toned features · one `span=2` feature.

**Mobile home screen.**
`<BentoGrid cols={2}>` with `span=2` for the hero and progress tiles and 1×1 for small stats. Stays 2 columns on phones.

**Settings page.**
Not every page needs a bento grid. Use `Card` (header, content, footer) in a single column for forms longer than a few fields.

## Page container

`.bk-container` gives a centred column, 1240px max (set `--container` to change it), with safe-area-aware 16px side padding.
