# Components

47 components and 8 illustrated characters, each with a live preview, HTML markup, React usage, a props table generated from the TypeScript source, and accessibility notes.

## Layout

- [Bento grid](components/bento-grid.md): the grid, tiles, spans, rows and tones
- [Card](components/card.md): header, action, content and footer for standalone content
- [Stack and Row](components/stack.md): spacing helpers
- [Separator](components/separator.md): horizontal and vertical rules
- [Media](components/media.md): aspect-ratio box for images and video

## Actions

- [Button](components/button.md): seven variants, seven sizes, loading, `asChild`
- [Button group](components/button-group.md): joined buttons and split buttons
- [Toggle](components/toggle.md): pressed buttons and segmented controls
- [Kbd](components/kbd.md): keyboard keys
- [Tooltip](components/tooltip.md): CSS-only labels on hover and focus

## Forms

- [Field](components/field.md): label, help text and error, wired automatically
- [Input](components/input.md), [Textarea](components/textarea.md), [Select](components/select.md)
- [Input group](components/input-group.md): icons and hints inside an input
- [Checkbox](components/checkbox.md), [Radio group](components/radio-group.md), [Choice card](components/choice-card.md), [Switch](components/switch.md)
- [Slider](components/slider.md), [Input OTP](components/input-otp.md), [Dropzone](components/dropzone.md), [Calendar](components/calendar.md)

## Data display

- [Badge](components/badge.md), [Avatar](components/avatar.md)
- [Table](components/table.md), [List](components/list.md)
- [Stat](components/stat.md) with sparkline, [Bar chart](components/bar-chart.md) with meter and legend, [Progress](components/progress.md) with ring
- [Accordion](components/accordion.md)

## Feedback

- [Alert](components/alert.md), [Toast](components/toast.md), [Empty state](components/empty.md), [Skeleton](components/skeleton.md), [Spinner](components/spinner.md)

## Overlays

- [Dialog](components/dialog.md), [Sheet](components/sheet.md), [Dropdown menu](components/dropdown-menu.md), [Popover](components/popover.md), [Command](components/command.md)

## Navigation

- [Tabs](components/tabs.md), [Breadcrumb](components/breadcrumb.md), [Pagination](components/pagination.md), [Navbar](components/navbar.md), [Sidebar](components/sidebar.md), [Bottom nav](components/bottom-nav.md)

## Illustrations

- [Characters](components/characters.md): eight pencil-drawn people and animals with six moods each, for empty states, errors, loading and success

## Conventions

- **HTML**: every component is markup plus `bk-` classes. Variants are `data-variant`, `data-size` and `data-tone` attributes. The optional script ([JavaScript API](javascript-api.md)) adds behaviour through `data-bk-*` attributes.
- **React**: `import { … } from 'bento-shad-ui/react'`. Every component forwards `ref` and passes unknown props (`id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event handlers) to its root element. Stateful components work controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`). Link-like components take `asChild` for router links.
- **Icons**: the library ships none. Any 24px stroke icon works; lucide-react matches best. In HTML, give inline SVGs `class="bk-icon"`; in React, pass the icon element, and SVGs inside buttons, menu items and similar are sized for you.

<!-- docs/javascript-api.md -->

# JavaScript API (core)

`import { … } from 'bento-shad-ui'` (ESM), or `window.BentoUI` from the script-tag build. Written in TypeScript; types ship in `dist/types`. Every function is safe to import during server rendering and does nothing there.

## Starting

```ts
start(options?: { observe?: boolean; restoreTheme?: boolean }): void
```

Attaches the delegated listeners (once), restores the saved theme, runs `init(document)` when the DOM is ready, and by default watches for added nodes. `import 'bento-shad-ui/auto'` and the script-tag build call it for you.

```ts
init(root?: ParentNode): void
```

Sets up widgets that need per-element work (tabs, command palettes, calendars, slider fills, `data-indeterminate` checkboxes) inside `root`. Safe to call repeatedly; each element is set up once. Call it after inserting HTML if you started with `observe: false`.

## Theme

```ts
type Theme = 'light' | 'dark' | 'system';
type ResolvedTheme = 'light' | 'dark';

setTheme(theme: Theme, options?: { persist?: boolean }): void   // sets data-theme + .dark, saves, fires bk:theme
getTheme(): Theme                                                // from <html data-theme>
resolveTheme(theme?: Theme): ResolvedTheme                       // 'system' → OS setting
getStoredTheme(): Theme | null                                   // localStorage 'bk-theme'
onThemeChange(listener: (d: { theme: Theme; resolved: ResolvedTheme }) => void): () => void
isTheme(value: unknown): value is Theme
themeScript: string          // inline <head> script that prevents a dark-mode flash
THEME_STORAGE_KEY = 'bk-theme'
THEME_EVENT = 'bk:theme'
```

## Toast

```ts
interface ToastOptions {
  title: string;
  description?: string;
  variant?: 'default' | 'success' | 'destructive';
  duration?: number;            // ms, default 4500; Infinity keeps it open
  action?: { label: string; onClick?: () => void };
}
toast(input: string | ToastOptions): () => void   // returns dismiss()
```

## Popovers

```ts
enablePopoverPlacement(): void                              // idempotent; start() calls it
placePopover(popover: HTMLElement, anchor?: HTMLElement): void
```

Kit popovers (`.bk-menu[popover]`, `.bk-popover[popover]`) are placed under the button whose `popovertarget` points at them, aligned by `data-align="start|center|end"`, flipped above when there's no room, and kept in place on scroll and resize.

## Other

```ts
openCommand(dialog?: HTMLDialogElement | null): void   // toggles a command dialog (default: dialog.bk-command[data-bk-hotkey])
fillSlider(range: HTMLInputElement): void              // updates --val and <output for>
version: string
```

## Events

| Event | Target | `detail` |
|---|---|---|
| `bk:theme` | `document` | `{ theme, resolved }` |
| `bk:change` | `[data-bk-tabs]` | `{ tab }`: the selected tab element |
| `bk:change` | `.bk-calendar` | `{ start, end }`: day-of-month numbers |

All events bubble.

## Data attributes

| Attribute | On | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `data-bk-theme-set` | button | `light` / `dark` / `system` |
| `data-bk-open` | button | id of a `<dialog>` to open |
| `data-bk-close` | inside a dialog | closes it; the value becomes `returnValue` |
| `data-bk-toast` | button | JSON `ToastOptions` or plain title text |
| `data-bk-copy` / `data-bk-copy-target` | button | text, or a selector whose text is copied |
| `data-bk-tabs` | wrapper | enables tabs |
| `data-bk-hotkey` | `dialog.bk-command` | ⌘K / Ctrl+K toggles it |
| `data-keep-open` | `.bk-menu-item` | don't close the menu on click |
| `data-indeterminate` | `.bk-checkbox` | sets `indeterminate` on init |
| `data-prefix` / `data-suffix` | `.bk-slider` | text around the `<output>` value |
| `data-bk-react` | any | marks React-managed elements; the core ignores them |

## Script-tag build

`dist/bento.iife.min.js` defines `window.BentoUI` with every export above and calls `start()` immediately.

```html
<script
    src="…/bento.iife.min.js"
    defer
></script>
<script>
    addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => BentoUI.toast('Ready'));
</script>
```

<!-- docs/accessibility.md -->

# Accessibility

The target is WCAG 2.2 AA. This page lists what the library does for you and what you still have to do.

## Built in

**Contrast, checked by tests.** `npm test` computes WCAG contrast for every text/background token pair in light and dark mode and fails the build below the limits:

- text pairs (`foreground`/`background`, `primary-foreground`/`primary`, `muted-foreground` on `background`, `card` and `muted`, every tint and its foreground, status colours on cards…): at least 4.5:1
- `--input` (form control borders) and `--ring` (focus ring) against `--card` and `--background`: at least 3:1

That's why `--destructive-foreground` exists: white text on dark mode's light red fails, so dark mode uses dark text.

**Focus.** Every interactive element shows a 3px ring in `--ring` on `:focus-visible`. Nothing removes outlines without a replacement.

**Keyboard.**

| Component | Keys |
|---|---|
| Tabs | ←/→ move and select, Home/End |
| Dropdown menu | opens with focus on the first item; ↑/↓, Home/End; Esc closes and returns focus |
| Popover | Esc closes; focus moves into it on open |
| Dialog / Sheet | focus trapped by the native `<dialog>`; Esc closes |
| Command palette | ⌘K/Ctrl+K; ↑/↓ and Enter; `aria-activedescendant` keeps the screen reader on the active option |
| Calendar | ←/→ day, ↑/↓ week; Enter or Space picks |
| Input OTP | digits only; Backspace goes back; ←/→; paste fills all slots |
| Toggle / Switch / Checkbox / Radio | native Space / arrow behaviour |
| Accordion | native `<details>`: Enter/Space |

**Semantics.** Native elements first (`<button>`, `<dialog>`, `<details>`, `<select>`, `<input type="range">`, `popover`). ARIA is added where native HTML has none: `aria-pressed` on toggles, `aria-current` on nav, `role="tab"`/`tabpanel` wiring, `role="alert"` on destructive alerts and toasts, `aria-busy` on loading buttons, `role="progressbar"` with values.

**Motion.** `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes animations and transitions.

**Forms.** The React `Field` connects label, help text and error (`htmlFor`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`).

## Your part

- **Name icon-only buttons**: `aria-label="Delete"`. A tooltip alone is not a name.
- **Describe charts**: `Sparkline` and `Ring` require `label`; give HTML charts an `aria-label` that states the values.
- **Image alt text** on `Avatar` and `Media` images.
- **Label every input.** Use `Field` or `<label for>`, and `aria-label` only when a visible label is impossible.
- **Don't rely on colour alone.** Badges and alerts carry text; keep it meaningful ("Paid", not just a green dot).
- **Keep the tone rules.** Custom token values must still meet the contrast limits above. Run `npm test` if you fork the tokens.
- **Language**: set `<html lang>`.
- **Toasts** disappear: don't put the only copy of important information or the only way to undo something in a toast.

<!-- docs/ai-agents.md -->

# Using bento-shad-ui with AI coding agents

The library ships documentation written for language models, so an agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex…) can build UIs with it correctly in any project.

Start with the [examples](examples.md) for complete dashboard, settings, pricing and onboarding compositions. These files are documentation, not an MCP server, and do not guarantee inclusion in model recommendations.

## Files for agents

| File | Use |
|---|---|
| `llms.txt` | Short index in the llmstxt.org format: what the library is, with links to every guide |
| `llms-full.txt` | Every guide and component page in one file. Give this to an agent that has to write UI code |

Where to find them:

- installed: `node_modules/bento-shad-ui/llms.txt` and `node_modules/bento-shad-ui/llms-full.txt`
- online: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SaadNiaziDev/bento-shad-ui/main/llms-full.txt`
- site: `https://saadniazidev.github.io/bento-shad-ui/llms-full.txt`

## Add this to the project's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / .cursorrules

```markdown
## UI: bento-shad-ui

This project's UI uses bento-shad-ui (https://github.com/SaadNiaziDev/bento-shad-ui).
Before writing UI code, read node_modules/bento-shad-ui/llms-full.txt.

- Layout pages as bento grids: BentoGrid + Tile (React) or .bk-bento > .bk-bento-grid > .bk-tile (HTML).
  One idea per tile; spans in a row add up to 4; at most one toned tile in four; one inverse tile per view.
- Use library components before writing new ones. React: import from 'bento-shad-ui/react'.
- Colours come only from tokens (var(--primary), var(--muted-foreground), var(--tint-peach)…). Never hard-code hex or Tailwind palette colours.
- Fonts: Red Hat Text (body) and Red Hat Display (headings). No monospace font anywhere, not even for code.
- Variants are props in React (variant, size, tone) and data attributes in HTML (data-variant, data-size, data-tone).
- Dark mode is automatic through tokens. Don't write dark: overrides for colours.
- Icon-only buttons need aria-label; charts need a label; inputs go inside <Field>.
- Use the styles ending in -foreground for text on a coloured surface.
```

## Prompts that work well

- "Build the settings page as a single `Card` with `Field`s and `Switch` rows, using bento-shad-ui/react."
- "Make the dashboard a 4-column `BentoGrid`: sidebar `rows={3}`, three `Stat` tiles, a `BarChart` tile `span={2}`, an activity `List` tile `rows={2}`, a `Table` tile `span={2}`."
- "Convert this page to bento-shad-ui HTML classes and the CDN script. Keep the copy."

## Check an agent's output

- No `#hex`, `rgb()` or Tailwind colour utilities (`bg-blue-500`) in new code; only tokens or `bg-tint-*`/`bg-brand` in shadcn projects.
- No `font-mono`, monospace font stacks, Inter, Geist or other fonts.
- Spans add up per row at 4 columns, and the page still reads at 2 and 1 columns.
- Every icon-only button has `aria-label`.

## Design decisions for this library

- Keep orange for primary emphasis. Most surfaces stay neutral; reserve tinted tiles for a specific grouping or status.
- Use motion to confirm an action or explain where a surface appeared. Keep command navigation immediate, and avoid decorative entrance sequences on routine screens.
- Gate hover movement to devices with a precise pointer. A touch interaction must work without a hover state.
- Check long project names, translated action labels, empty lists and large amounts at narrow container widths. Never hide an essential action to make a demo fit.
- Keep human-readable examples: four spaces per nesting level, clean HTML element boundaries and copyable source with preserved whitespace. Run `npm run docs:format` after editing examples.

These are bento-shad-ui decisions, informed by Emil Kowalski’s public writing on [purposeful motion](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/you-dont-need-animations), [interaction details](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/7-practical-animation-tips) and [articulating design decisions for agents](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/agents-with-taste). They do not require his skill pack or add a motion dependency.

<!-- docs/components/bento-grid.md -->

# Bento grid

> The layout at the heart of the library. Tiles span columns and rows; the grid follows its container's width, not the viewport.

```html
<div class="bk-bento">
    <div class="bk-bento-grid">
        <article
            class="bk-tile bk-span-2 bk-row-2"
            data-tone="inverse"
        >
            <span class="bk-eyebrow">Next trip</span>
            <h3 class="bk-h3">Lisbon in 12 days</h3>
            <p
                class="bk-muted"
                style="margin: 0"
            >
                4 nights · 2 travellers · Chiado
            </p>
        </article>
        <article
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="peach"
        >
            <span class="bk-eyebrow">Budget</span>
            <span class="bk-num">€640</span>
        </article>
        <article class="bk-tile">
            <span class="bk-eyebrow">Weather</span>
            <span class="bk-num">18°</span>
        </article>
        <article
            class="bk-tile bk-span-2"
            data-tone="sky"
        >
            <span class="bk-eyebrow">Packing list</span>
            <div
                class="bk-progress"
                role="progressbar"
                aria-label="Packing list"
                aria-valuenow="68"
                aria-valuemin="0"
                aria-valuemax="100"
            >
                <span style="--v: 68%"></span>
            </div>
        </article>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
    BentoGrid,
    Tile,
    TileHeader,
    TileTitle,
    TileDescription,
    TileFooter,
    Eyebrow,
} from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<BentoGrid>
    <Tile
        span={2}
        rows={2}
        tone="inverse"
    >
        <Eyebrow>Next trip</Eyebrow>
        <TileTitle>Lisbon in 12 days</TileTitle>
    </Tile>
    <Tile tone="peach">…</Tile>
    <Tile>…</Tile>
    <Tile span={2}>…</Tile>
</BentoGrid>;
```

```html
<div class="bk-bento">
    <div class="bk-bento-grid">
        <article
            class="bk-tile bk-span-2 bk-row-2"
            data-tone="inverse"
        >
            …
        </article>
        <article
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="peach"
        >
            …
        </article>
    </div>
</div>
```

The outer `.bk-bento` is the box the grid measures (a container query container). `BentoGrid` renders both elements for you.

## Examples

### Tile anatomy

```html
<div class="bk-bento">
    <div
        class="bk-bento-grid"
        data-cols="2"
    >
        <article class="bk-tile">
            <header class="bk-tile-header">
                <div>
                    <h3 class="bk-tile-title">Bookings</h3>
                    <p class="bk-tile-description">This week · 330 total</p>
                </div>
                <span
                    class="bk-badge"
                    data-variant="secondary"
                >
                    Week
                </span>
            </header>
            <p
                class="bk-muted"
                style="margin: 0"
            >
                Content goes here.
            </p>
            <footer class="bk-tile-footer">
                <span class="bk-muted">Updated 2m ago</span>
                <button
                    class="bk-button"
                    data-size="xs"
                    type="button"
                >
                    Open
                </button>
            </footer>
        </article>
        <a
            class="bk-tile"
            data-interactive
            data-tone="mint"
            href="#tile-anatomy"
        >
            <h3 class="bk-tile-title">Clickable tile</h3>
            <p
                class="bk-tile-description"
                style="margin: 0"
            >
                data-interactive lifts it on hover.
            </p>
        </a>
    </div>
</div>
```

### Tones

```html
<div class="bk-bento">
    <div class="bk-bento-grid">
        <div
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="muted"
        >
            muted
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="peach"
        >
            peach
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="sky"
        >
            sky
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="mint"
        >
            mint
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="lilac"
        >
            lilac
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="butter"
        >
            butter
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="inverse"
        >
            inverse
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-tile"
            data-tone="brand"
        >
            brand
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
```

Components placed inside a toned tile pick up matching colours, so buttons, inputs and badges stay readable.

## API

### BentoGrid

<!-- props: BentoGridProps -->

### Tile

<!-- props: TileProps -->

Parts: `TileHeader`, `TileTitle` (h3), `TileDescription`, `TileFooter` (pinned to the bottom), `TileMedia` (bleeds to the top edge), `Eyebrow`. Each renders one element with its class and accepts that element's attributes.

### HTML

| Class or attribute | Effect |
|---|---|
| `bk-bento` | Container the grid measures |
| `bk-bento-grid` | The grid. `data-cols="2"`, `"3"`, `"6"` change the full-width column count |
| `bk-tile` | A tile |
| `bk-span-2`, `bk-span-3`, `bk-span-4`, `bk-span-full` | Column span |
| `bk-row-2`, `bk-row-3` | Row span |
| `data-tone` | `muted` `peach` `sky` `mint` `lilac` `butter` `inverse` `brand` |
| `data-interactive`, `data-center` | Hover lift; centred content |

Columns: 4 above 900px of container width, 2 down to 560px, 1 below. `data-cols="2"` keeps 2 columns down to 300px. See [Layout](../layout.md) for the rules.

## Accessibility

- Tiles are layout only. Use real headings inside (`TileTitle` is an `h3`) so screen-reader users can jump between them.
- Visual order follows source order except where dense packing fills gaps. Keep the reading order sensible in the markup.
- A clickable tile should be one link (`asChild` with an `<a>`), not a `div` with a click handler.

<!-- docs/components/card.md -->

# Card

> shadcn/ui card anatomy (header, action, content, footer) for content outside a bento grid, such as forms and settings.

```html
<div
    class="bk-card"
    style="width: 340px"
>
    <div class="bk-card-header">
        <h3 class="bk-card-title">Lisbon, 4 nights</h3>
        <div class="bk-card-action">
            <span
                class="bk-badge"
                data-variant="success"
                data-dot
            >
                Booked
            </span>
        </div>
        <p class="bk-card-description">12–16 March · 2 travellers</p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-content">
        <p
            class="bk-muted"
            style="margin: 0"
        >
            Hotel Chiado, breakfast included, free cancellation until 10 March.
        </p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-footer">
        <span class="bk-large">€640</span>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-size="sm"
            type="button"
        >
            View plan
        </button>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
    Card,
    CardHeader,
    CardTitle,
    CardDescription,
    CardAction,
    CardContent,
    CardFooter,
    Badge,
    Button,
} from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Card>
    <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Lisbon, 4 nights</CardTitle>
        <CardAction>
            <Badge
                variant="success"
                dot
            >
                Booked
            </Badge>
        </CardAction>
        <CardDescription>12–16 March · 2 travellers</CardDescription>
    </CardHeader>
    <CardContent>…</CardContent>
    <CardFooter>
        <span>€640</span>
        <Button size="sm">View plan</Button>
    </CardFooter>
</Card>;
```

## When to use Card or Tile

- **Tile** is a cell of a bento grid: large radius, no shadow, sized by the grid.
- **Card** stands on its own: forms, settings sections, a detail panel next to a list. It has a light shadow and inner padding per section.

## Examples

### Project summary

Keep the status next to the title, with one primary action in the footer.

```html
<article
    class="bk-card"
    style="width: 100%; max-width: 400px"
>
    <div class="bk-card-header">
        <h3 class="bk-card-title">Website refresh</h3>
        <div class="bk-card-action">
            <span
                class="bk-badge"
                data-variant="outline"
            >
                In progress
            </span>
        </div>
        <p class="bk-card-description">Studio North · Design team</p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-content bk-stack">
        <div class="bk-row bk-between">
            <span class="bk-small">Milestones</span>
            <span class="bk-caption">3 of 4 complete</span>
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-progress"
            role="progressbar"
            aria-label="Project milestones"
            aria-valuenow="75"
            aria-valuemin="0"
            aria-valuemax="100"
        >
            <span style="--v: 75%"></span>
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-avatar-group"
            aria-label="Team members: Sam, Alex, Noor"
        >
            <span class="bk-avatar">SK</span>
            <span class="bk-avatar">AL</span>
            <span class="bk-avatar">NK</span>
        </div>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-footer">
        <span class="bk-caption">Due December 12</span>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-size="sm"
            type="button"
            data-bk-toast='{"title":"Project preview","description":"Connect your project navigation here."}'
        >
            View project
        </button>
    </div>
</article>
```

### Account preferences

A form card groups related fields. This preview demonstrates local feedback; save and validate values in your application before showing success.

```html

    class="bk-card"

                class="bk-label"
                for="card-language"
            >

            </label>

                class="bk-select"

                <option>French</option>

                class="bk-switch"
                type="checkbox"
                role="switch"
                checked

```

### Subscription card

Use a badge for context and readable billing terms near the price.

### Notification card

A compact card works well for a single update, with supporting actions that wrap on small screens.

```html
        >
            Preview export
        </button>
    </div>
</article>
```

### Empty card

An empty state can sit inside the same card shell as its eventual content.

```html
<section
    class="bk-card"
    style="width: 100%; max-width: 440px"
    aria-labelledby="card-files-title"
>
    <div class="bk-card-header">

            class="bk-card-title"
            id="card-files-title"

        </h3>

        </p>

            <span class="bk-empty-icon">

                    class="bk-icon"
                    aria-hidden="true"

                </svg>
            </span>

            <p class="bk-empty-description">
                Add a brief, reference or draft to get started.
            </p>
            <div class="bk-empty-actions">
                <label
                    class="bk-button"
                    data-variant="outline"
                >
                    Choose a file
                    <input
                        class="bk-sr-only"
                        type="file"
                        aria-label="Choose a project file"
                    />
                </label>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>
</section>
```

The file picker is local only; selecting a file does not upload it.

### Long content in a narrow card

Names and contact addresses should remain readable when they are longer than the demo data. Resize this preview: the title wraps, the contact address breaks only when necessary, and footer actions can wrap onto their own line. Try it in both themes.

```html
<article
    class="bk-card"
    style="width: 100%; max-width: 320px"
>
    <div class="bk-card-header">
        <h3 class="bk-card-title">
            Northwind International Research &amp; Development
        </h3>
        <p class="bk-card-description">
            أمينة عبد الرحمن · Workspace administrator
        </p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-content">
        <p class="bk-card-description">
            amina.abdulrahman@northwind-research.example.com
        </p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-card-footer">
        <span class="bk-caption">1 pending invitation</span>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
            data-bk-toast='{"title":"Invitation preview","description":"No invitation was sent."}'

            Preview invitation reminder
        </button>
    </div>
</article>
```

## API

Every part renders one element and accepts that element's attributes:

| Part | Element | Class |
|---|---|---|
| `Card` | `div` | `bk-card` |
| `CardHeader` | `div` | `bk-card-header` |
| `CardTitle` | `h3` | `bk-card-title` |
| `CardDescription` | `p` | `bk-card-description` |
| `CardAction` | `div` | `bk-card-action` (top right of the header) |
| `CardContent` | `div` | `bk-card-content` |
| `CardFooter` | `div` | `bk-card-footer` |

## Accessibility

- `CardTitle` is an `h3`. If the page outline needs another level, use a heading with the class instead: `<h2 className="bk-card-title">`.

<!-- docs/components/media.md -->

# Media

> An aspect-ratio box for images and video, with an optional caption chip.

```html
<div
    class="bk-media"
    style="
        --ratio: 16 / 10;
        width: 340px;
        background: linear-gradient(var(--tint-sky), var(--card));
    "
>
    <span class="bk-media-caption">Alfama, Lisbon</span>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Media } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Media
    ratio="4 / 3"
    caption="Alfama, Lisbon"
>
    <img
        src="/alfama.jpg"
        alt="Rooftops of Alfama at sunset"
    />
</Media>;
```

```html
<div
    class="bk-media"
    style="--ratio: 4 / 3"
>
    <img
        src="/alfama.jpg"
        alt="Rooftops of Alfama at sunset"
    />
    <span class="bk-media-caption">Alfama, Lisbon</span>
</div>
```

The image or video fills the box with `object-fit: cover`. Inside a tile, `TileMedia` (`.bk-tile-media`) makes it bleed to the tile's top edges.

## API

<!-- props: MediaProps -->

## Accessibility

- Write `alt` text that says what the image shows. Use `alt=""` for decorative images.

# Separator

> A thin horizontal or vertical rule between groups of content.

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="width: 300px"
>
    <span class="bk-small">Itinerary</span>
    <hr class="bk-separator" />
    <div
        class="bk-row"
        style="--gap: 12px; height: 20px"
    >
        <span class="bk-muted">Day 1</span>
        <hr
            class="bk-separator"
            data-orientation="vertical"
        />
        <span class="bk-muted">Day 2</span>
        <hr
            class="bk-separator"
            data-orientation="vertical"
        />
        <span class="bk-muted">Day 3</span>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Separator } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Separator />
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
```

## API

<!-- props: SeparatorProps -->

| HTML | Effect |
|---|---|
| `<hr class="bk-separator">` | Horizontal |
| `<hr class="bk-separator" data-orientation="vertical">` | Vertical, stretches to the row height |

<!-- docs/components/stack.md -->

# Stack and Row

> Small flex helpers for vertical and horizontal spacing inside tiles and cards.

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="--gap: 10px; width: 280px"
>
    <div class="bk-row bk-between">
        <span class="bk-label">Total</span>
        <span class="bk-large">€640</span>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-row"
        style="--gap: 6px"
    >
        <span class="bk-badge">Booked</span>
        <span
            class="bk-badge"
            data-variant="outline"
        >
            4 nights
        </span>
    </div>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-block
        type="button"
    >
        View plan
    </button>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Stack, Row } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Stack gap={10}>
    <Row between>
        <span>Total</span>
        <span>€640</span>
    </Row>
    <Row gap={6}>…</Row>
</Stack>;
```

## API

### Stack

<!-- props: StackProps -->

### Row

<!-- props: RowProps -->

### HTML

| Class | Effect |
|---|---|
| `bk-stack` | Column, gap `var(--gap, 12px)` |
| `bk-row` | Wrapping row, centred, gap `var(--gap, 8px)` |
| `bk-between` | Push children to both ends |
| `bk-grow` | Take the remaining space (`flex: 1`, `min-width: 0`) |
| `bk-container` | Centred page column, 1240px max (`--container`), safe-area padding |
| `bk-truncate` | One line with an ellipsis |
| `bk-sr-only` | Hidden visually, read by screen readers |

<!-- docs/components/button.md -->

# Button

> Triggers an action. Seven variants, seven sizes, icon, loading and disabled states, and asChild for links.

```html
<div class="bk-row">
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        type="button"
    >
        Book trip
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="brand"
        type="button"
    >
        Upgrade
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        type="button"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-plus" />
        </svg>
        Add trip
    </button>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';
import Link from 'next/link';

<Button onClick={book}>Book trip</Button>
<Button variant="outline" size="sm">
    <Plus />
    Add trip
</Button>
<Button asChild variant="link">
    <Link href="/terms">View terms</Link>
</Button>
```

```html
<button
    class="bk-button"
    type="button"
>
    Book trip
</button>
<button
    class="bk-button"
    data-variant="outline"
    data-size="sm"
>
    …
</button>
<a
    class="bk-button"
    data-variant="link"
    href="/terms"
>
    View terms
</a>
```

## Examples

### Variants

```html
<div class="bk-row">
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        type="button"
    >
        Default
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="brand"
        type="button"
    >
        Brand
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="secondary"
        type="button"
    >
        Secondary
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        type="button"
    >
        Outline
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="ghost"
        type="button"
    >
        Ghost
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="destructive"
        type="button"
    >
        Delete
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="link"
        type="button"
    >
        Link
    </button>
</div>
```

### Sizes

```html
<div class="bk-row">
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-size="xs"
        type="button"
    >
        Extra small
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-size="sm"
        type="button"
    >
        Small
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        type="button"
    >
        Default
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-size="lg"
        type="button"
    >
        Large
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        data-size="icon-sm"
        type="button"
        aria-label="Edit"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-pencil" />
        </svg>
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        data-size="icon"
        type="button"
        aria-label="Download"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-download" />
        </svg>
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-size="icon-lg"
        type="button"
        aria-label="Add"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            data-size="lg"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-plus" />
        </svg>
    </button>
</div>
```

### Loading and disabled

```html
<div class="bk-row">
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-loading
        disabled
        aria-busy="true"
        type="button"
    >
        <span
            class="bk-spinner"
            data-size="sm"
            aria-hidden="true"
        ></span>
        Saving
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        disabled
        type="button"
    >
        Disabled
    </button>
</div>
```

```tsx
<Button loading>Saving</Button>;
```

### Full width

```html
<button
    class="bk-button"
    data-block
    data-size="lg"
    type="button"
>
    Create account
</button>
```

## API

<!-- props: ButtonProps -->

### HTML

| Attribute | Values |
|---|---|
| `data-variant` | `brand` `secondary` `outline` `ghost` `destructive` `link` (omit for default) |
| `data-size` | `xs` `sm` `lg` `icon` `icon-sm` `icon-lg` (omit for default) |
| `data-loading` | Dims the button and blocks clicks. Add a `.bk-spinner` and `disabled` |
| `data-block` | Full width |

## Accessibility

- Icon-only buttons need `aria-label`. A tooltip doesn't count as a name.
- `loading` sets `disabled` and `aria-busy`. Keep the label (for example "Saving") so the state is announced.
- Use `asChild` with a link for navigation. Buttons perform actions; links go places.
- The default `type` is `button`, so a button inside a form doesn't submit it by accident. Set `type="submit"` when it should.

<!-- docs/components/button-group.md -->

# Button group

> Buttons joined into one control, including the split-button pattern.

```html
<div
    class="bk-row"
    style="--gap: 16px"
>
    <div
        class="bk-button-group"
        role="group"
        aria-label="Range"
    >
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            data-size="sm"
            type="button"
        >
            Day
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            data-size="sm"
            type="button"
        >
            Week
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            data-size="sm"
            type="button"
        >
            Month
        </button>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-button-group">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-size="sm"
            type="button"
        >
            Save draft
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-size="icon-sm"
            type="button"
            aria-label="More save options"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-chevron-down" />
            </svg>
        </button>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { ButtonGroup, Button } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<ButtonGroup aria-label="Range">
    <Button
        variant="outline"
        size="sm"
    >
        Day
    </Button>
    <Button
        variant="outline"
        size="sm"
    >
        Week
    </Button>
    <Button
        variant="outline"
        size="sm"
    >
        Month
    </Button>
</ButtonGroup>;
```

For a split button, put a `DropdownMenu` trigger in the second slot. For a choice that stays selected, use a [Toggle group](toggle.md) instead.

## API

`ButtonGroup` renders `<div role="group" class="bk-button-group">` and accepts all `div` attributes. Give it an `aria-label`.

## Accessibility

- `role="group"` plus `aria-label` tells screen readers the buttons belong together.
- Each button still needs its own visible text or `aria-label`.

<!-- docs/components/kbd.md -->

# Kbd

> Keyboard keys and shortcuts, shown inline in text, menus and inputs.

```html
<p
    class="bk-muted"
    style="margin: 0"
>
    Press
    <span class="bk-kbd-group">
        <kbd class="bk-kbd">⌘</kbd>
        <kbd class="bk-kbd">K</kbd>
    </span>
    to search, or
    <span class="bk-kbd-group">
        <kbd class="bk-kbd">Ctrl</kbd>
        +
        <kbd class="bk-kbd">K</kbd>
    </span>
    on Windows.
</p>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<KbdGroup>
    <Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
    <Kbd>K</Kbd>
</KbdGroup>;
```

```html
<span class="bk-kbd-group">
    <kbd class="bk-kbd">⌘</kbd>
    <kbd class="bk-kbd">K</kbd>
</span>
```

## API

`Kbd` renders `<kbd class="bk-kbd">`; `KbdGroup` renders `<span class="bk-kbd-group">`. Both accept their element's attributes. Keys use the sans font: the library has no monospace face.

<!-- docs/components/toggle.md -->

# Toggle

> A button that stays pressed. Toggle groups make segmented controls with one or many choices.

```html
<div
    class="bk-row"
    style="--gap: 16px"
>
    <div
        class="bk-row"
        style="--gap: 4px"
    >
        <button
            class="bk-toggle"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
            aria-pressed="true"
            aria-label="Bold"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-bold" />
            </svg>
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-toggle"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
            aria-pressed="false"
            aria-label="Italic"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-italic" />
            </svg>
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-toggle"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
            aria-pressed="false"
            aria-label="Underline"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-underline" />
            </svg>
        </button>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-toggle-group"
        data-type="single"
        role="group"
        aria-label="Alignment"
    >
        <button
            class="bk-toggle"
            type="button"
            aria-pressed="true"
            aria-label="Align left"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-align-left" />
            </svg>
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-toggle"
            type="button"
            aria-pressed="false"
            aria-label="Align center"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-align-center" />
            </svg>
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-toggle"
            type="button"
            aria-pressed="false"
            aria-label="Align right"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-align-right" />
            </svg>
        </button>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Toggle, ToggleGroup } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Toggle
    variant="outline"
    aria-label="Bold"
    pressed={bold}
    onPressedChange={setBold}
>
    <Bold />
</Toggle>

<ToggleGroup type="single" defaultValue="left" aria-label="Alignment">
    <Toggle value="left" aria-label="Align left">
        <AlignLeft />
    </Toggle>
    <Toggle value="center" aria-label="Align center">
        <AlignCenter />
    </Toggle>
</ToggleGroup>

<ToggleGroup
    type="multiple"
    value={styles}
    onValueChange={setStyles}
    aria-label="Text style"
>
    …
</ToggleGroup>
```

In HTML, the script flips `aria-pressed` on click. `data-type="single"` keeps exactly one pressed.

## API

### Toggle

<!-- props: ToggleProps -->

### ToggleGroup

<!-- props: ToggleGroupProps -->

## Accessibility

- State is exposed with `aria-pressed`, which screen readers announce as "pressed" or "not pressed".
- Icon-only toggles need `aria-label`; the group needs `aria-label` too.

<!-- docs/components/tooltip.md -->

# Tooltip

> A short text label shown on hover and keyboard focus. Pure CSS, no script needed.

```html
<div class="bk-row">
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        data-size="icon"
        type="button"
        aria-label="Copy link"
        data-bk-tooltip="Copy link"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-link" />
        </svg>
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        data-size="icon"
        type="button"
        aria-label="Add to favourites"
        data-bk-tooltip="Add to favourites"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-heart" />
        </svg>
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        data-size="icon"
        type="button"
        aria-label="Delete"
        data-bk-tooltip="Delete"
        data-bk-tooltip-side="bottom"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-trash" />
        </svg>
    </button>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Tooltip, Button } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Tooltip content="Copy link">
    <Button
        variant="outline"
        size="icon"
        aria-label="Copy link"
    >
        <Link2 />
    </Button>
</Tooltip>;
```

```html
<button
    class="bk-button"
    aria-label="Copy link"
    data-bk-tooltip="Copy link"
    data-bk-tooltip-side="bottom"
>
    …
</button>
```

## API

<!-- props: TooltipProps -->

## Accessibility

- The tooltip is drawn by CSS from the attribute, so screen readers don't read it. Always give the element an accessible name (`aria-label` or visible text).
- It appears on keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`) as well as hover.
- Plain text only. For links or buttons inside a floating panel, use a [Popover](popover.md).

# Calendar

> Month calendar for picking one day or a range, with keyboard navigation and localised names.

```html
<div
    class="bk-calendar"
    data-mode="range"
    aria-label="March 2026"
>

            class="bk-button"

```

Click two days to pick a range. The HTML version is static markup that the script makes selectable; the React component also builds the month and moves between months.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Calendar, type DateRange } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange | null>(null);

<Calendar mode="range" value={range} onValueChange={setRange} />

<Calendar
    defaultValue={new Date()}
    isDisabled={(d) => d < startOfToday}
    weekStartsOn={0}
    locale="pt-PT"
/>
```

Helpers for building your own views: `getMonthGrid(year, month, weekStartsOn)` returns the 42 days of a month (6 weeks, with outside days), `toDateKey(date)` gives `YYYY-MM-DD` in local time, and `isSameDay(a, b)` compares dates.

## API

<!-- props: CalendarProps -->

In HTML, `data-mode="range"` enables range picking and the calendar fires `bk:change` with `{ start, end }` day numbers.

## Accessibility

- Arrow keys move by day (←/→) and week (↑/↓); Enter or Space picks.
- Each day has a full label ("Thursday 12 March 2026") and `aria-pressed` when selected.
- The month title is a live region, so month changes are announced.

<!-- docs/components/checkbox.md -->

# Checkbox

> Native checkbox with checked, unchecked and indeterminate states, with optional label and description.

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="width: 300px"
>
    <label class="bk-option">
        <input
            class="bk-checkbox"
            type="checkbox"
            data-indeterminate
        />
        <span class="bk-option-text"><span>All extras</span></span>
    </label>
    <label class="bk-option">
        <input
            class="bk-checkbox"
            type="checkbox"
            checked
        />
        <span class="bk-option-text">
            <span>Window seat</span>
            <span>Free on flights over 2 hours</span>
        </span>
    </label>
    <label class="bk-option">
        <input
            class="bk-checkbox"
            type="checkbox"
        />
        <span class="bk-option-text">
            <span>Extra checked bag</span>
            <span>€35 each way</span>
        </span>
    </label>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Checkbox
    label="Window seat"
    description="Free on flights over 2 hours"
    defaultChecked
/>
<Checkbox
    label="All extras"
    indeterminate={some && !all}
    checked={all}
    onCheckedChange={setAll}
/>
<Checkbox aria-label="Select row" />
```

With `label`, the checkbox is wrapped in a clickable `<label class="bk-option">` row. Without it, you get the bare input.

## API

<!-- props: CheckboxProps -->

### HTML

| Class or attribute | Use |
|---|---|
| `bk-checkbox` | The input |
| `bk-option` / `bk-option-text` | Label row; first span is the label, second the description |
| `data-indeterminate` | The script sets `indeterminate` on load |

## Accessibility

- Space toggles. The whole label row is clickable.
- `indeterminate` is announced as "mixed".

<!-- docs/components/choice-card.md -->

# Choice card

> A selectable card holding a radio or checkbox, for plans, shipping options and similar choices.

```html
<fieldset class="bk-fieldset">
    <legend>Plan</legend>
    <div class="bk-form-row">
        <label class="bk-choice">
            <input
                class="bk-radio"
                type="radio"
                name="cc-plan"
                checked
            />
            <span class="bk-option-text">
                <span>Free</span>
                <span>3 trips, 1 traveller</span>
            </span>
            <span class="bk-choice-price">€0</span>
        </label>
        <label class="bk-choice">
            <input
                class="bk-radio"
                type="radio"
                name="cc-plan"
            />
            <span class="bk-option-text">
                <span>Plus</span>
                <span>Unlimited trips, 6 travellers</span>
            </span>
            <span class="bk-choice-price">€4/mo</span>
        </label>
    </div>
</fieldset>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { RadioGroup, ChoiceCard } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<RadioGroup legend="Plan" defaultValue="free">
    <ChoiceCard
        value="free"
        label="Free"
        description="3 trips, 1 traveller"
        aside="€0"
    />
    <ChoiceCard
        value="plus"
        label="Plus"
        description="Unlimited trips, 6 travellers"
        aside="€4/mo"
    />
</RadioGroup>

<ChoiceCard type="checkbox" label="Travel insurance" aside="€12" />
```

## API

<!-- props: ChoiceCardProps -->

The selected card gets a 2px outline in `--foreground` through `:has(:checked)`.

## Accessibility

- The whole card is the label, so clicking anywhere selects it. Keyboard behaviour is the native radio or checkbox behaviour.

<!-- docs/components/dropzone.md -->

# Dropzone

> Drag-and-drop file area backed by a real file input, so click and keyboard work too.

```html
<label
    class="bk-dropzone"
    style="width: 340px"
>
    <input
        type="file"
        multiple
        accept="image/*,.pdf"
    />
    <svg
        class="bk-icon"
        data-size="lg"
        aria-hidden="true"
    >
        <use href="#i-upload" />
    </svg>
    <span class="bk-small">Drop files or click to upload</span>
    <span class="bk-caption">PNG, JPG or PDF, up to 10 MB</span>
    <span class="bk-dropzone-files"></span>
</label>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Dropzone } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';
import { Upload } from 'lucide-react';

<Dropzone
    multiple
    accept="image/*,.pdf"
    icon={<Upload />}
    hint="PNG, JPG or PDF, up to 10 MB"
    onFiles={(files) => upload(files)}
/>;
```

The component shows the drag-over state and the chosen file names. Size and type limits are up to your upload code: `accept` is only a hint to the file picker.

## API

<!-- props: DropzoneProps -->

## Accessibility

- The real `<input type="file">` covers the zone, so it's reachable with Tab and opens with Enter or Space.
- Announce upload results (success or errors) with a [Toast](toast.md) or an [Alert](alert.md).

<!-- docs/components/field.md -->

# Field

> Label, control, help text and error message, with ids and ARIA wired for you.

```html
<div
    class="bk-form"
    style="width: 320px"
>
    <div class="bk-field">
        <label
            class="bk-label"
            for="fd-email"
        >
            Email
        </label>
        <input
            class="bk-input"
            id="fd-email"
            type="email"
            placeholder="you@example.com"
            aria-describedby="fd-email-d"
        />
        <p
            class="bk-field-description"
            id="fd-email-d"
        >
            We'll send the itinerary here.
        </p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-field">
        <label
            class="bk-label"
            for="fd-code"
        >
            Promo code
        </label>
        <input
            class="bk-input"
            id="fd-code"
            value="SUMMER"
            aria-invalid="true"
            aria-describedby="fd-code-e"
        />
        <p
            class="bk-field-error"
            id="fd-code-e"
        >
            This code expired on 31 August.
        </p>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Field
    label="Email"
    description="We'll send the itinerary here."
    error={errors.email}
    required
>
    <Input
        type="email"
        name="email"
    />
</Field>;
```

`Field` generates an id (or uses yours), connects `<label for>`, points `aria-describedby` at the description and error, sets `aria-invalid` when there's an error, and passes `required` to the control. It works with any single control: `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Slider`.

### With react-hook-form

```tsx
<Field
    label="Email"
    error={formState.errors.email?.message}
>
    <Input
        type="email"
        {...register('email', { required: 'Enter your email' })}
    />
</Field>;
```

## Examples

### Form layout

```html
<form
    class="bk-form"
    onsubmit="event.preventDefault()"
>
    <div class="bk-form-row">
        <div class="bk-field">
            <label
                class="bk-label"
                for="fl-first"
            >
                First name
            </label>
            <input
                class="bk-input"
                id="fl-first"
                autocomplete="given-name"
            />
        </div>
        <div class="bk-field">
            <label
                class="bk-label"
                for="fl-last"
            >
                Last name
            </label>
            <input
                class="bk-input"
                id="fl-last"
                autocomplete="family-name"
            />
        </div>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-field">
        <label
            class="bk-label"
            for="fl-mail"
        >
            Email
        </label>
        <input
            class="bk-input"
            id="fl-mail"
            type="email"
            autocomplete="email"
        />
    </div>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        type="submit"
    >
        Create account
    </button>
</form>
```

### Validation with a recovery path

Submit an empty or malformed email to see an inline error, then correct it and submit again. This example uses native email validity and keeps the message next to the field. A valid value is acknowledged locally; it does not create an account or send an email.

```html
<form
    class="bk-form"
    id="contact-example"
    novalidate
>
    <div class="bk-field">
        <label
            class="bk-label"
            for="contact-email"
        >
            Work email
        </label>
        <input
            class="bk-input"
            id="contact-email"
            name="email"
            type="email"
            required
            autocomplete="email"
            aria-describedby="contact-email-help"
        />
        <p
            class="bk-field-description"
            id="contact-email-help"
        >
            Use an address where your team can reach you.
        </p>
        <p
            class="bk-field-error"
            id="contact-email-error"
            hidden
        ></p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-row">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            type="submit"
        >
            Check email
        </button>
        <span class="bk-caption">Preview only · nothing is sent</span>
    </div>
    <p
        class="bk-field-description"
        role="status"
        data-contact-status
    ></p>
</form>
```

The preview uses this handler. Validation runs on submit, rather than interrupting someone while they type.

```js
const form = document.querySelector('#contact-example');
const email = form.elements.namedItem('email');
const error = form.querySelector('#contact-email-error');
const status = form.querySelector('[data-contact-status]');

form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const invalid = !email.validity.valid;
    email.setAttribute('aria-invalid', String(invalid));
    email.setAttribute(
        'aria-describedby',
        invalid
            ? 'contact-email-help contact-email-error'
            : 'contact-email-help',
    );
    error.hidden = !invalid;
    error.textContent = email.validity.valueMissing
        ? 'Enter your work email to continue.'
        : 'Enter a complete email address, such as sam@example.com.';
    status.textContent = invalid
        ? ''
        : 'Email format checked. Nothing was sent.';
    if (invalid) email.focus();
});
```

## API

<!-- props: FieldProps -->

### HTML

| Class | Use |
|---|---|
| `bk-field` | Wrapper: label, control, help, error (8px gap) |
| `bk-label` | Label text |
| `bk-field-description` | Help text, linked with `aria-describedby` |
| `bk-field-error` | Error text, linked with `aria-describedby`; set `aria-invalid="true"` on the control |
| `bk-form` | Vertical stack of fields (16px gap) |
| `bk-form-row` | Fields side by side, wrapping below 160px each |
| `bk-fieldset` | Unstyled `<fieldset>` with a styled `<legend>` |

## Accessibility

- Every control needs a label. Use `aria-label` only when a visible label is impossible.
- Show errors after the user leaves the field or submits, not on every keystroke.
- Errors say what's wrong and how to fix it ("This code expired on 31 August"), not just "Invalid".

<!-- docs/components/input.md -->

# Input

> Single-line text input. Supports every native type, with focus, invalid and disabled states.

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="width: 300px"
>
    <input
        class="bk-input"
        type="email"
        placeholder="you@example.com"
        aria-label="Email"
    />
    <input
        class="bk-input"
        value="SUMMER"
        aria-invalid="true"
        aria-label="Promo code"
    />
    <input
        class="bk-input"
        value="Read only, disabled"
        disabled
        aria-label="Disabled example"
    />
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Input, Field } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Field label="Email">
    <Input type="email" name="email" />
</Field>
<Input invalid aria-label="Promo code" />
```

```html
<input
    class="bk-input"
    type="email"
    aria-label="Email"
/>
```

## API

<!-- props: InputProps -->

The input is 40px tall with a 3px focus ring in `--ring`. Its border uses `--input`, which is tested to reach 3:1 contrast against the card and the page.

## Accessibility

- Pair it with a label: `Field`, `<label for>`, or `aria-label`.
- Use the right `type` and `autocomplete` (`email`, `tel`, `one-time-code`…) so phones show the right keyboard and autofill works.
- Use `aria-invalid` (or `invalid`) together with a visible error message, never colour alone.

<!-- docs/components/input-group.md -->

# Input group

> An input with an icon at the start and a hint or button at the end, such as a search field.

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="width: 320px"
>
    <div class="bk-input-group">
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-search" />
        </svg>
        <input
            class="bk-input"
            type="search"
            placeholder="Search trips"
            aria-label="Search trips"
        />
        <span class="bk-input-end bk-kbd-group">
            <kbd class="bk-kbd">⌘</kbd>
            <kbd class="bk-kbd">K</kbd>
        </span>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-input-group">
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-map-pin" />
        </svg>
        <input
            class="bk-input"
            value="Lisbon, Portugal"
            aria-label="Location"
        />
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { InputGroup, Input, KbdGroup, Kbd } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';
import { Search } from 'lucide-react';

<InputGroup
    icon={<Search />}
    end={
        <KbdGroup>
            <Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
            <Kbd>K</Kbd>
        </KbdGroup>
    }
>
    <Input
        type="search"
        placeholder="Search trips"
        aria-label="Search trips"
    />
</InputGroup>;
```

## API

<!-- props: InputGroupProps -->

| HTML | Use |
|---|---|
| `bk-input-group` | Wrapper |
| `.bk-icon` or `bk-input-start` | Leading icon; the input gets extra left padding |
| `bk-input-end` | Trailing content, for example a `bk-kbd-group` or an icon button |

## Accessibility

- The icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`). The input still needs a label or `aria-label`.

<!-- docs/components/input-otp.md -->

# Input OTP

> One-time code entry: digits only, auto-advance, backspace to go back, and paste to fill every slot.

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="width: 320px"
>
    <div
        class="bk-otp"
        role="group"
        aria-label="Verification code"
    >
        <div class="bk-otp-group">
            <input
                inputmode="numeric"
                maxlength="1"
                aria-label="Digit 1"
            />
            <input
                inputmode="numeric"
                maxlength="1"
                aria-label="Digit 2"
            />
            <input
                inputmode="numeric"
                maxlength="1"
                aria-label="Digit 3"
            />
        </div>
        <span
            class="bk-otp-separator"
            aria-hidden="true"
        ></span>
        <div class="bk-otp-group">
            <input
                inputmode="numeric"
                maxlength="1"
                aria-label="Digit 4"
            />
            <input
                inputmode="numeric"
                maxlength="1"
                aria-label="Digit 5"
            />
            <input
                inputmode="numeric"
                maxlength="1"
                aria-label="Digit 6"
            />
        </div>
    </div>
    <p class="bk-field-description">
        Type or paste the 6-digit code sent to m•••@example.com.
    </p>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { InputOTP } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<InputOTP
    groups={[3, 3]}
    aria-label="Verification code"
    onComplete={(code) => verify(code)}
/>
<InputOTP
    groups={[4]}
    value={pin}
    onValueChange={setPin}
    aria-label="PIN"
/>
```

## API

<!-- props: InputOTPProps -->

## Accessibility

- Each slot has a label ("Digit 2 of 6"); the group has `aria-label`.
- The first slot uses `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so phones can fill codes from SMS.
- ←/→ move between slots; Backspace on an empty slot goes back.

<!-- docs/components/radio-group.md -->

# Radio group

> One choice from a short list, as a native fieldset of radios.

```html
<fieldset
    class="bk-radio-group"
    style="width: 260px"
>
    <legend
        class="bk-label"
        style="margin-bottom: 4px"
    >
        Cabin class
    </legend>
    <label class="bk-option">
        <input
            class="bk-radio"
            type="radio"
            name="rg-cabin"
            checked
        />
        <span>Economy</span>
    </label>
    <label class="bk-option">
        <input
            class="bk-radio"
            type="radio"
            name="rg-cabin"
        />
        <span>Premium economy</span>
    </label>
    <label class="bk-option">
        <input
            class="bk-radio"
            type="radio"
            name="rg-cabin"
        />
        <span>Business</span>
    </label>
</fieldset>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { RadioGroup, Radio } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<RadioGroup
    legend="Cabin class"
    value={cabin}
    onValueChange={setCabin}
>
    <Radio
        value="economy"
        label="Economy"
    />
    <Radio
        value="premium"
        label="Premium economy"
    />
    <Radio
        value="business"
        label="Business"
        description="Lie-flat seats"
    />
</RadioGroup>;
```

`RadioGroup` gives every `Radio` the same `name` and keeps the value. For radios that look like cards, use [Choice card](choice-card.md) inside the same group.

## API

### RadioGroup

<!-- props: RadioGroupProps -->

### Radio

<!-- props: RadioProps -->

## Accessibility

- Arrow keys move between radios in a group; Tab moves in and out of the group (native behaviour).
- The `legend` names the group. Use `aria-label` on `RadioGroup` if you hide it.

<!-- docs/components/select.md -->

# Select

> A styled native select. The most reliable choice on phones, with screen readers and in forms.

```html
<div
    class="bk-field"
    style="width: 280px"
>
    <label
        class="bk-label"
        for="sl-dest"
    >
        Destination
    </label>
    <select
        class="bk-select"
        id="sl-dest"
    >
        <optgroup label="Portugal">
            <option>Lisbon</option>
            <option>Porto</option>
        </optgroup>
        <optgroup label="Spain">
            <option>Madrid</option>
            <option>Seville</option>
        </optgroup>
    </select>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Field, Select } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Field label="Destination">
    <Select
        value={city}
        onChange={(e) => setCity(e.target.value)}
    >
        <optgroup label="Portugal">
            <option>Lisbon</option>
            <option>Porto</option>
        </optgroup>
    </Select>
</Field>;
```

The open list is the operating system's own picker, so it works with touch, keyboard and screen readers everywhere. For a searchable list, use a [Command](command.md) inside a [Popover](popover.md).

## API

<!-- props: SelectProps -->

<!-- docs/components/slider.md -->

# Slider

> Pick a number in a range. A native range input with a filled track and a live value.

```html
<div
    class="bk-field"
    style="width: 300px"
>
    <div class="bk-row bk-between">
        <label
            class="bk-label"
            for="sd-price"
        >
            Max nightly price
        </label>
        <output
            class="bk-small"
            for="sd-price"
        >
            €140
        </output>
    </div>
    <input
        class="bk-slider"
        id="sd-price"
        type="range"
        min="40"
        max="400"
        step="10"
        value="140"
        data-prefix="€"
    />
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Field, Slider } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

const [price, setPrice] = useState(140);
<Field label={`Max nightly price: €${price}`}>
    <Slider
        min={40}
        max={400}
        step={10}
        value={price}
        onValueChange={setPrice}
    />
</Field>;
```

In HTML, the script keeps the filled part of the track (`--val`) and any `<output for="id">` in sync. `data-prefix` and `data-suffix` add text around the value.

## API

<!-- props: SliderProps -->

## Accessibility

- Native range input: arrow keys step, Page Up/Down jump, Home/End go to the ends.
- Show the current value as text (an `<output>` or the label) so it isn't conveyed by position alone.

<!-- docs/components/switch.md -->

# Switch

> An on/off control for settings that apply immediately.

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="width: 300px"
>
    <label class="bk-switch-row">
        <span class="bk-option-text">
            <span>Price alerts</span>
            <span>When a saved fare drops</span>
        </span>
        <input
            class="bk-switch"
            type="checkbox"
            role="switch"
            checked
        />
    </label>
    <label class="bk-switch-row">
        <span>Offline maps</span>
        <input
            class="bk-switch"
            type="checkbox"
            role="switch"
            data-tone="brand"
            checked
        />
    </label>
    <label class="bk-switch-row">
        <span>Share location</span>
        <input
            class="bk-switch"
            type="checkbox"
            role="switch"
        />
    </label>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Switch } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Switch
    label="Price alerts"
    description="When a saved fare drops"
    checked={alerts}
    onCheckedChange={setAlerts}
/>
<Switch tone="brand" aria-label="Offline maps" />
```

With `label`, the switch sits at the end of a full-width clickable row.

## API

<!-- props: SwitchProps -->

## Accessibility

- It's a native checkbox with `role="switch"`, so screen readers announce "on" or "off". Space toggles it.
- Use a switch only for changes that take effect at once. Inside a form that needs saving, use a checkbox.

<!-- docs/components/accordion.md -->

# Accordion

> Collapsible sections built on native details and summary, so they work before JavaScript loads.

```html
<div class="bk-accordion">
    <details
        class="bk-accordion-item"
        open
    >
        <summary class="bk-accordion-trigger">Can I change my dates?</summary>
        <div class="bk-accordion-content">
            Yes. Change them up to 48 hours before check-in at no cost.
        </div>
    </details>
    <details class="bk-accordion-item">
        <summary class="bk-accordion-trigger">
            How do shared payments work?
        </summary>
        <div class="bk-accordion-content">
            Each traveller pays their share by card. The booking is confirmed
            when the last share is paid.
        </div>
    </details>
    <details class="bk-accordion-item">
        <summary class="bk-accordion-trigger">
            Do the maps work offline?
        </summary>
        <div class="bk-accordion-content">
            On Plus, yes. Download a city from the trip page before you leave.
        </div>
    </details>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Accordion>
    <AccordionItem
        title="Can I change my dates?"
        defaultOpen
    >
        Yes, up to 48 hours before check-in.
    </AccordionItem>
    <AccordionItem
        title="How do shared payments work?"
        onOpenChange={(open) => track(open)}
    >
        …
    </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>;
```

To allow only one open item at a time, give the items the same `name` attribute (supported by current browsers for `<details>`).

## API

<!-- props: AccordionItemProps -->

## Accessibility

- Native `<details>`: Enter or Space toggles, and screen readers announce expanded or collapsed.
- Browser find-in-page opens closed sections that contain the match.

<!-- docs/components/avatar.md -->

# Avatar

> A person's photo or initials, with sizes, a status dot and overlapping groups.

```html
<div
    class="bk-row"
    style="--gap: 16px"
>
    <span
        class="bk-avatar"
        data-size="sm"
    >
        MK
    </span>
    <span
        class="bk-avatar"
        data-status="online"
    >
        JR
    </span>
    <span
        class="bk-avatar"
        data-size="lg"
        data-status="busy"
    >
        AS
    </span>
    <span
        class="bk-avatar"
        data-size="xl"
        data-shape="square"
    >
        LT
    </span>
    <span class="bk-avatar-group">
        <span
            class="bk-avatar"
            style="
                background: var(--tint-peach);
                color: var(--tint-peach-foreground);
            "
        >
            MK
        </span>
        <span
            class="bk-avatar"
            style="
                background: var(--tint-sky);
                color: var(--tint-sky-foreground);
            "
        >
            JR
        </span>
        <span
            class="bk-avatar"
            style="
                background: var(--tint-mint);
                color: var(--tint-mint-foreground);
            "
        >
            AS
        </span>
        <span class="bk-avatar">+3</span>
    </span>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Avatar
    src={user.photo}
    alt={user.name}
    fallback="MK"
    size="lg"
    status="online"
/>
<AvatarGroup>
    <Avatar fallback="MK" />
    <Avatar fallback="JR" />
    <Avatar fallback="+3" />
</AvatarGroup>
```

If the image fails to load, `fallback` is shown instead.

## API

<!-- props: AvatarProps -->

## Accessibility

- Give photos `alt` text with the person's name, unless the name is already written next to the avatar (then use `alt=""`).
- The status dot is visual only. Say the status in text nearby if it matters.

```html
<span
```

<!-- docs/components/bar-chart.md -->

# Bar chart

> A to-scale bar chart drawn with CSS, plus a meter for parts of a whole and a legend.

```html
<div
    class="bk-chart"
    role="img"
    aria-label="Bookings per day: Mon 32, Tue 45, Wed 28, Thu 52, Fri 61, Sat 74, Sun 38"
>
    <div class="bk-bars">
        <div
            class="bk-bar"
            data-muted
            style="--v: 40%"
            data-value="32"
        ></div>
        <div
            class="bk-bar"
            data-muted
            style="--v: 56.25%"
            data-value="45"
        ></div>
        <div
            class="bk-bar"
            data-muted
            style="--v: 35%"
            data-value="28"
        ></div>
        <div
            class="bk-bar"
            data-muted
            style="--v: 65%"
            data-value="52"
        ></div>
        <div
            class="bk-bar"
            data-muted
            style="--v: 76.25%"
            data-value="61"
        ></div>
        <div
            class="bk-bar"
            style="--v: 92.5%"
            data-value="74"
            data-show
        ></div>
        <div
            class="bk-bar"
            data-muted
            style="--v: 47.5%"
            data-value="38"
        ></div>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-bar-labels">
        <span>Mon</span>
        <span>Tue</span>
        <span>Wed</span>
        <span>Thu</span>
        <span>Fri</span>
        <span>Sat</span>
        <span>Sun</span>
    </div>
</div>
```

The scale tops out at 80, and gridlines mark 20, 40 and 60. Hover a bar to see its value.

## Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<BarChart
    data={[
        { label: 'Mon', value: 32 },
        { label: 'Tue', value: 45 },
        { label: 'Sat', value: 74 },
    ]}
    max={80}
    formatValue={(v) => `${v} bookings`}
/>;
```

`BarChart` computes each bar's height from `max` (or the largest value), emphasises the highest bar and writes an `aria-label` listing every value. `barHeights(data, max)` returns the percentages if you need them.

## Meter and legend

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="width: 320px"
>
    <div
        class="bk-meter"
        role="img"
        aria-label="Stay 46%, travel 22%, food 12%, unspent 20%"
    >
        <span style="--v: 46%; --c: var(--chart-1)"></span>
        <span style="--v: 22%; --c: var(--chart-2)"></span>
        <span style="--v: 12%; --c: var(--chart-3)"></span>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-legend">
        <span style="--c: var(--chart-1)">Stay 46%</span>
        <span style="--c: var(--chart-2)">Travel 22%</span>
        <span style="--c: var(--chart-3)">Food 12%</span>
        <span style="--c: var(--muted)">Unspent 20%</span>
    </div>
</div>
```

```tsx
import { Meter, Legend } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

const parts = [
    { label: 'Stay', value: 46, color: 'var(--chart-1)' },
    { label: 'Travel', value: 22, color: 'var(--chart-2)' },
];

<Meter segments={parts} />
<Legend
    items={parts.map((p) => ({
        label: `${p.label} ${p.value}%`,
        color: p.color,
    }))}
/>
```

## API

### BarChart

<!-- props: BarChartProps -->

### Meter

<!-- props: MeterProps -->

For line, area or stacked charts, use a chart library (Recharts, Chart.js) with the `--chart-1` to `--chart-5` tokens so colours match both themes.

## Accessibility

- Charts render as `role="img"` with a text summary. Keep the summary specific: the values, not "a chart".
- Don't rely on colour alone to tell series apart; label them in a legend or in text.
