<!-- docs/components/progress.md -->

# Progress

> Linear progress bars in three tones, and a ring for a single percentage.

```html
<div
    class="bk-row"
    style="--gap: 28px"
>
    <div
        class="bk-stack"
        style="width: 260px; --gap: 14px"
    >
        <div
            class="bk-progress"
            role="progressbar"
            aria-label="Packing list"
            aria-valuenow="68"
            aria-valuemin="0"
            aria-valuemax="100"
        >
            <span style="--v: 68%"></span>
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-progress"
            data-tone="brand"
            role="progressbar"
            aria-label="Upload"
            aria-valuenow="40"
            aria-valuemin="0"
            aria-valuemax="100"
        >
            <span style="--v: 40%"></span>
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-progress"
            data-tone="success"
            role="progressbar"
            aria-label="Done"
            aria-valuenow="100"
            aria-valuemin="0"
            aria-valuemax="100"
        >
            <span style="--v: 100%"></span>
        </div>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-ring"
        style="--p: 71"
        role="img"
        aria-label="71% of budget used"
    >
        <span aria-hidden="true">71%</span>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Progress, Ring } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Progress value={17} max={25} label="Packing list" />
<Progress value={uploaded} tone="brand" label="Upload" />
<Ring value={71} size={64} label="71% of budget used" />
```

## API

### Progress

<!-- props: ProgressProps -->

### Ring

<!-- props: RingProps -->

## Accessibility

- `Progress` sets `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`; `label` names it.
- `Ring` is a picture of one number: its `label` should state that number and what it means.

<!-- docs/components/stat.md -->

# Stat

> A key number with its label, a change versus a previous period, and an optional sparkline.

```html
<div
    class="bk-tile"
    style="width: 300px"
>
    <div class="bk-stat">
        <span class="bk-stat-label">Bookings this month</span>
        <span class="bk-stat-value">1,284</span>
        <span
            class="bk-stat-delta"
            data-trend="up"
        >
            +12.4% vs February
        </span>
    </div>
    <svg
        class="bk-spark"
        viewBox="0 0 100 32"
        preserveAspectRatio="none"
        role="img"
        aria-label="Bookings rose from 12 to 31 a day over the week"
    >
        <polygon
            points="0,30 16.67,21.16 33.33,25.58 50,15.26 66.67,19.68 83.33,7.89 100,2 100,32 0,32"
        />
        <polyline
            points="0,30 16.67,21.16 33.33,25.58 50,15.26 66.67,19.68 83.33,7.89 100,2"
        />
        <circle
            cx="100"
            cy="2"
            r="2.5"
        />
    </svg>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Stat, Sparkline } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Stat
    label="Bookings this month"
    value="1,284"
    delta="+12.4% vs February"
    trend="up"
    icon={<Calendar />}
/>
<Sparkline
    data={[12, 18, 15, 22, 19, 27, 31]}
    label="Bookings rose from 12 to 31 a day over the week"
/>
```

`Sparkline` scales the line to the data's own minimum and maximum. `sparklinePoints(data, width, height, padding)` returns the coordinates if you draw your own.

## Examples

### A balanced metric row

A bento grid stacks the metrics automatically when its container becomes narrow. Include the direction and comparison period in the text, not only the colour.

```html
<div class="bk-bento">
    <div class="bk-bento-grid">
        <article class="bk-tile bk-span-2">
            <div class="bk-stat">
                <span class="bk-stat-label">Monthly revenue</span>
                <span class="bk-stat-value">$24,680</span>
                <span
                    class="bk-stat-delta"
                    data-trend="up"
                >
                    +18.6% vs last month
                </span>
            </div>
        </article>
        <article class="bk-tile bk-span-2">
            <div class="bk-stat">
                <span class="bk-stat-label">Cancelled subscriptions</span>
                <span class="bk-stat-value">18</span>
                <span
                    class="bk-stat-delta"
                    data-trend="down"
                >
                    −6 vs last month
                </span>
            </div>
        </article>
    </div>
</div>
```

### A quiet summary

Omit the trend when a comparison would not be meaningful.

```html
<article
    class="bk-card"
    style="width: 100%; max-width: 340px"
>
    <div class="bk-card-content">
        <div class="bk-stat">
            <span class="bk-stat-label">Available storage</span>
            <span class="bk-stat-value">84 GB</span>
            <span class="bk-caption">Of 100 GB on your current plan</span>
        </div>
    </div>
</article>
```

## API

### Stat

<!-- props: StatProps -->

### Sparkline

<!-- props: SparklineProps -->

## Accessibility

- `trend` only changes colour; write the direction in `delta` ("+12.4%", "−3 pts").
- `Sparkline` requires `label`: describe what the line shows, because the shape alone is invisible to screen readers.

<!-- docs/components/table.md -->

# Table

> A data table that scrolls sideways inside its wrapper on narrow screens, with tabular numbers.

```html
<div class="bk-table-wrap">
    <table class="bk-table">
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Guest</th>
                <th>Trip</th>
                <th>Status</th>
                <th data-align="end">Amount</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td>Maya Kim</td>
                <td>Lisbon</td>
                <td>
                    <span
                        class="bk-badge"
                        data-variant="success"
                    >
                        Paid
                    </span>
                </td>
                <td data-align="end">€640.00</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td>Jonas Ruiz</td>
                <td>Porto</td>
                <td>
                    <span
                        class="bk-badge"
                        data-variant="warning"
                    >
                        Pending
                    </span>
                </td>
                <td data-align="end">€410.00</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td>Amira Saleh</td>
                <td>Seville</td>
                <td>
                    <span
                        class="bk-badge"
                        data-variant="outline"
                    >
                        Draft
                    </span>
                </td>
                <td data-align="end">€385.50</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
        <caption>3 bookings this week</caption>
    </table>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
    Table,
    TableHeader,
    TableBody,
    TableRow,
    TableHead,
    TableCell,
    TableCaption,
} from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Table>
    <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
            <TableHead>Guest</TableHead>
            <TableHead align="end">Amount</TableHead>
        </TableRow>
    </TableHeader>
    <TableBody>
        {rows.map((r) => (
            <TableRow key={r.id}>
                <TableCell>{r.guest}</TableCell>
                <TableCell align="end">{r.amount}</TableCell>
            </TableRow>
        ))}
    </TableBody>
    <TableCaption>3 bookings this week</TableCaption>
</Table>;
```

For sorting, filtering and paging, drive these parts from a headless table library such as TanStack Table, and add [Pagination](pagination.md).

### Empty results

Keep the table headings visible and span the empty row across every column. Filtering logic belongs to your application.

```html

                        </p>
                    </div>
                </td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>
</div>
```

## API

### Table

<!-- props: TableProps -->

### TableHead and TableCell

<!-- props: TableCellProps -->

`TableHeader`, `TableBody`, `TableFooter`, `TableRow` and `TableCaption` render their elements unchanged.

## Accessibility

- Use `TableHead` (`<th scope="col">`) for column headers and a `TableCaption` that says what the table shows.
- Right-align numbers with `align="end"` so digits line up.

<!-- docs/components/alert.md -->

# Alert

> An inline message about the current page, in five variants, with optional actions.

```html
<div class="bk-stack">
    <div
        class="bk-alert"
        role="status"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-info" />
        </svg>
        <div class="bk-alert-title">Flight time changed</div>
        <div class="bk-alert-description">
            TP 1351 now leaves at 09:15, 35 minutes later.
        </div>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-alert"
        data-variant="success"
        role="status"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-check-circle" />
        </svg>
        <div class="bk-alert-title">Booking confirmed</div>
        <div class="bk-alert-description">Everyone has paid their share.</div>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-alert"
        data-variant="warning"
        role="status"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-triangle" />
        </svg>
        <div class="bk-alert-title">Passport expires soon</div>
        <div class="bk-alert-description">
            Some countries need 6 months of validity.
        </div>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-alert"
        data-variant="destructive"
        role="alert"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-alert" />
        </svg>
        <div class="bk-alert-title">Payment failed</div>
        <div class="bk-alert-description">
            Your card was declined. Update it to keep the booking.
        </div>
        <div class="bk-alert-actions">
            <button
                class="bk-button"
                data-variant="destructive"
                data-size="xs"
                type="button"
            >
                Update card
            </button>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Alert, Button } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';
import { TriangleAlert } from 'lucide-react';

<Alert
    variant="warning"
    icon={<TriangleAlert />}
    title="Passport expires soon"
    actions={<Button size="xs">Renew</Button>}
>
    Some countries need 6 months of validity.
</Alert>;
```

Variants: `default`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`.

## API

<!-- props: AlertProps -->

## Accessibility

- `destructive` uses `role="alert"`, so screen readers announce it right away; the others use `role="status"`, which is announced politely.
- Use an alert for information about the page that stays until it's resolved. For short confirmations, use a [Toast](toast.md).

<!-- docs/components/empty.md -->

# Empty state

> What to show when there's nothing yet. Say what will appear here and how to add the first item.

```html
<div class="bk-empty">
    <span class="bk-empty-icon">
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            data-size="lg"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-plane" />
        </svg>
    </span>
    <h4 class="bk-empty-title">No trips yet</h4>
    <p class="bk-empty-description">
        Trips you plan or get invited to show up here. Start with a city and
        dates.
    </p>
    <div class="bk-empty-actions">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            type="button"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-plus" />
            </svg>
            Plan a trip
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
        >
            Import booking
        </button>
    </div>
</div>
```

### With a character

```html
<div class="bk-empty">
    <div class="bk-empty-illustration">
        <span
            class="bk-illustration"
            data-bk-character="pip"
            data-mood="thinking"
        ></span>
    </div>
    <h4 class="bk-empty-title">No results for "Lisbn"</h4>
    <p class="bk-empty-description">
        Check the spelling, or search for a country instead of a city.
    </p>
    <div class="bk-empty-actions">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
        >
            Clear search
        </button>
    </div>
</div>
```

See [Characters](characters.md) for the whole cast.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Empty, Button } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';
import { Plane, Plus } from 'lucide-react';

<Empty
    icon={<Plane />}
    title="No trips yet"
    description="Trips you plan or get invited to show up here. Start with a city and dates."
    actions={
        <Button>
            <Plus />
            Plan a trip
        </Button>
    }
/>

<Empty
    illustration={<PencilCharacter character="pip" mood="thinking" />}
    title='No results for "Lisbn"'
    description="Check the spelling, or search for a country instead of a city."
/>
```

## Examples

### No search results

Explain how someone can recover. Connect the button to your filter state in a real application.

```html
<div class="bk-empty">
    <span class="bk-empty-icon">
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-search" />
        </svg>
    </span>
    <h4 class="bk-empty-title">No matching projects</h4>
    <p class="bk-empty-description">
        Try a shorter name or remove a filter to see more projects.
    </p>
    <div class="bk-empty-actions">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
            data-bk-toast='{"title":"Filter preview","description":"Reset your application filters here."}'
        >
            Preview filter reset
        </button>
    </div>
</div>
```

### All caught up

An empty state can confirm a good outcome without adding an unnecessary action.

```html
<div class="bk-empty">
    <span class="bk-empty-icon">
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-check-circle" />
        </svg>
    </span>
    <h4 class="bk-empty-title">You’re all caught up</h4>
    <p class="bk-empty-description">
        New notifications will appear here when your team shares an update.
    </p>
</div>
```

## API

<!-- props: EmptyProps -->

## Writing it

- Title: what's missing ("No trips yet"), not "Nothing here".
- Description: what will show up here and how to get there.
- One primary action. Use a second outline button only for a real alternative.

<!-- docs/components/skeleton.md -->

# Skeleton

> A pulsing placeholder that holds the layout while content loads.

```html
<div
    class="bk-stack"
    style="width: 300px"
    aria-busy="true"
    aria-label="Loading booking"
>
    <div
        class="bk-row"
        style="flex-wrap: nowrap; --gap: 10px"
    >
        <span
            class="bk-skeleton"
            style="width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 50%"
        ></span>
        <div
            class="bk-stack bk-grow"
            style="--gap: 6px"
        >
            <span
                class="bk-skeleton"
                style="height: 12px; width: 70%"
            ></span>
            <span
                class="bk-skeleton"
                style="height: 12px; width: 45%"
            ></span>
        </div>
    </div>
    <span
        class="bk-skeleton"
        style="height: 72px; border-radius: var(--radius-xl)"
    ></span>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<div
    aria-busy="true"
    aria-label="Loading booking"
>
    <Skeleton
        width={40}
        height={40}
        circle
    />
    <Skeleton width="70%" />
    <Skeleton height={72} />
</div>;
```

## API

<!-- props: SkeletonProps -->

## Accessibility

- Skeletons are `aria-hidden`. Put `aria-busy="true"` and a label on the region that's loading.
- Shape skeletons like the real content, so the page doesn't jump when it arrives.
- The pulse stops when the user prefers reduced motion.

<!-- docs/components/spinner.md -->

# Spinner

> A small loading indicator that takes the current text colour.

```html
<div
    class="bk-row"
    style="--gap: 20px"
>
    <span
        class="bk-spinner"
        data-size="sm"
        role="status"
        aria-label="Loading"
    ></span>
    <span
        class="bk-spinner"
        role="status"
        aria-label="Loading"
    ></span>
    <span
        class="bk-spinner"
        data-size="lg"
        role="status"
        aria-label="Loading"
        style="color: var(--brand)"
    ></span>
    <span class="bk-row bk-muted">
        <span
            class="bk-spinner"
            data-size="sm"
            aria-hidden="true"
        ></span>
        Checking availability
    </span>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Spinner } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Spinner />
<Spinner size="lg" label="Loading trips" />
<span>
    <Spinner size="sm" label="" /> Checking availability
</span>
```

Inside a button, use `<Button loading>` instead.

## API

<!-- props: SpinnerProps -->

## Accessibility

- With a `label`, the spinner is a `status` that screen readers announce. Next to visible text, pass `label=""` to hide it from them.

<!-- docs/components/toast.md -->

# Toast

> A short, temporary message in the corner of the screen, called from code with no provider needed.

```html
<div class="bk-row">
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        type="button"
        data-bk-toast='{"title":"Trip saved","description":"Lisbon, 12–16 March","variant":"success"}'
    >
        Success
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        type="button"
        data-bk-toast='{"title":"Payment failed","description":"Your card was declined.","variant":"destructive"}'
    >
        Error
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="ghost"
        type="button"
        data-bk-toast='{"title":"Link copied"}'
    >
        Default
    </button>
</div>
```

## Usage

```ts
import { toast } from 'bento-shad-ui/react'; // or 'bento-shad-ui', or window.BentoUI.toast

toast('Link copied');

toast({
    title: 'Trip saved',
    description: 'Lisbon, 12–16 March',
    variant: 'success',
});

const dismiss = toast({
    title: 'Payment failed',
    variant: 'destructive',
    action: { label: 'Retry', onClick: retry },
    duration: 8000,
});
dismiss(); // close early
```

```html
<button
    class="bk-button"
    data-bk-toast='{"title":"Saved","variant":"success"}'
>
    Save
</button>
```

Toasts stack in the bottom-right corner, pause while hovered, while a control inside has keyboard focus, or while the tab is hidden. They close after 4.5 seconds of unpaused time. `duration: Infinity` keeps one open until it's dismissed.

## Examples

### Archive with Undo

Try archiving the file, then choose Undo in the toast. The file is removed from this preview and restored in its original position if you undo. Nothing is sent to a server. A real application should confirm the archive operation before showing success and offer recovery if the request fails.

```html
<div
    id="archive-example"
    class="bk-stack"
>
    <div
        class="bk-row bk-between"
        data-file
    >
        <div>
            <strong>Brand guidelines.pdf</strong>
            <p class="bk-caption">Updated today · 2.4 MB</p>
        </div>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
            data-archive
        >
            Archive
        </button>
    </div>
    <p
        class="bk-muted"
        role="status"
        data-archive-status
    >
        No changes in this preview.
    </p>
</div>
```

The same code below powers this preview. Load the vanilla core script before it, or import `toast` from the package in a bundled application.

```js
const example = document.querySelector('#archive-example');
const row = example.querySelector('[data-file]');
const status = example.querySelector('[data-archive-status]');

example.querySelector('[data-archive]').addEventListener('click', () => {
    row.hidden = true;
    status.textContent = 'File archived in this preview.';

    window.BentoUI.toast({
        title: 'File archived',
        description: 'Brand guidelines.pdf',
        duration: 8000,
        action: {
            label: 'Undo',
            onClick: () => {
                row.hidden = false;
                status.textContent = 'File restored.';
            },
        },
    });
});
```

### Persistent connection notice

Use a persistent message when the condition is still active. Close it when connectivity returns; important connection information should also be available inline.

```html
<button
    class="bk-button"
    data-variant="outline"
    type="button"
    id="offline-notice-example"
>
    Preview connection notice
</button>
```

```js
const button = document.querySelector('#offline-notice-example');
let dismissPrevious;

button.addEventListener('click', () => {
    dismissPrevious?.();
    const dismissOfflineNotice = window.BentoUI.toast({
        title: 'You’re offline',
        description: 'Changes will sync when your connection returns.',
        duration: Infinity,
    });

    // Call when your application confirms that connectivity is restored.
    window.addEventListener('online', dismissOfflineNotice, { once: true });
    dismissPrevious = () => {
        window.removeEventListener('online', dismissOfflineNotice);
        dismissOfflineNotice();
    };
});
```

## API

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | required | The message |
| `description` | `string` | – | Second line |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'success' \| 'destructive'` | `'default'` | Icon and colour |
| `duration` | `number` | `4500` | Milliseconds; `Infinity` keeps it open |
| `action` | `{ label: string; onClick?: () => void }` | – | One button; clicking it also closes the toast |

`toast()` returns a function that closes the toast. On the server it does nothing.

## Accessibility

- The container is a polite live region; destructive toasts use `role="alert"`.
- Toasts disappear. Don't make a toast the only place for important information or the only way to undo something.

<!-- docs/components/command.md -->

# Command

> A searchable list of actions and pages with keyboard navigation, inline or as a ⌘K palette.

```html
<div
    class="bk-command"
    data-inline
>
    <div class="bk-command-search">
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-search" />
        </svg>
        <input
            class="bk-command-input"
            placeholder="Type a command or search"
            aria-label="Command"
        />
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-command-list"
        role="listbox"
    >
        <div class="bk-command-group">
            <div class="bk-command-group-heading">Trips</div>
            <div
                class="bk-command-item"
                role="option"
            >
                <svg
                    class="bk-icon"
                    aria-hidden="true"
                >
                    <use href="#i-plane" />
                </svg>
                Lisbon, 12–16 March
            </div>
            <div
                class="bk-command-item"
                role="option"
            >
                <svg
                    class="bk-icon"
                    aria-hidden="true"
                >
                    <use href="#i-plane" />
                </svg>
                Porto, 2–5 April
            </div>
        </div>
        <div class="bk-command-group">
            <div class="bk-command-group-heading">Actions</div>
            <div
                class="bk-command-item"
                role="option"
                data-keywords="new create"
            >
                <svg
                    class="bk-icon"
                    aria-hidden="true"
                >
                    <use href="#i-plus" />
                </svg>
                New trip
                <span class="bk-kbd-group"><kbd class="bk-kbd">N</kbd></span>
            </div>
            <div
                class="bk-command-item"
                role="option"
                data-keywords="preferences"
            >
                <svg
                    class="bk-icon"
                    aria-hidden="true"
                >
                    <use href="#i-sliders" />
                </svg>
                Settings
            </div>
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-command-empty"
            hidden
        >
            No results.
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
```

Type to filter. This site's own search (⌘K) is the same component.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Command, CommandDialog } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

const groups = [
    {
        heading: 'Trips',
        items: [
            {
                id: 'lis',
                label: 'Lisbon, 12–16 March',
                keywords: ['portugal'],
                onSelect: () => router.push('/trips/lis'),
            },
        ],
    },
    {
        heading: 'Actions',
        items: [
            {
                id: 'new',
                label: 'New trip',
                shortcut: ['N'],
                onSelect: createTrip,
            },
        ],
    },
];

<Command groups={groups} />;

const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); // ⌘K / Ctrl+K toggles it
<CommandDialog
    open={open}
    onOpenChange={setOpen}
    groups={groups}
/>;
```

`filterCommandGroups(groups, query)` is exported if you build your own list.

### HTML

```html
<button
    class="bk-button"
    data-bk-open="cmd"
>
    Search
</button>
<dialog
    class="bk-command"
    id="cmd"
    data-bk-hotkey
    aria-label="Search"
>
    <div class="bk-command-search">
        <input
            class="bk-command-input"
            aria-label="Search"
        />
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-command-list"
        role="listbox"
    >
        <div class="bk-command-group">
            <div class="bk-command-group-heading">Trips</div>
            <a
                class="bk-command-item"
                role="option"
                href="/trips/lisbon"
                data-keywords="portugal"
            >
                Lisbon
            </a>
        </div>
        <div
            class="bk-command-empty"
            hidden
        >
            No results.
        </div>
    </div>
</dialog>
```

`data-bk-hotkey` makes ⌘K / Ctrl+K open it. Items can be links or have click handlers; `data-keywords` adds hidden search terms.

## API

### Command

<!-- props: CommandProps -->

### CommandDialog

<!-- props: CommandDialogProps -->

## Accessibility

- The input is a combobox that controls the list. `aria-activedescendant` points at the highlighted option, so screen readers follow it while focus stays in the input.
- ↑/↓ move, Enter runs the highlighted item, Esc closes the dialog.

<!-- docs/components/dialog.md -->

# Dialog

> A modal window on the native dialog element, with focus trapping, Esc to close and an alert variant for confirmations.

```html
<div class="bk-row">
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        type="button"
        data-bk-open="dg-edit"
    >
        Edit profile
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="destructive"
        type="button"
        data-bk-open="dg-delete"
    >
        Delete trip
    </button>
</div>
<dialog
    class="bk-dialog"
    id="dg-edit"
    aria-labelledby="dg-edit-t"
>
    <button
        class="bk-button bk-dialog-close"
        data-variant="ghost"
        data-size="icon-sm"
        type="button"
        data-bk-close
        aria-label="Close"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-x" />
        </svg>
    </button>
    <div class="bk-dialog-header">
        <h2
            class="bk-dialog-title"
            id="dg-edit-t"
        >
            Edit profile
        </h2>
        <p class="bk-dialog-description">Your name shows on shared trips.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-dialog-body">
        <div class="bk-field">
            <label
                class="bk-label"
                for="dg-name"
            >
                Name
            </label>
            <input
                class="bk-input"
                id="dg-name"
                value="Maya Kim"
                autofocus
            />
        </div>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-dialog-footer">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
            data-bk-close
        >
            Cancel
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            type="button"
            data-bk-close
            data-bk-toast='{"title":"Profile saved","variant":"success"}'
        >
            Save
        </button>
    </div>
</dialog>
<dialog
    class="bk-dialog"
    data-variant="alert"
    id="dg-delete"
    role="alertdialog"
    aria-labelledby="dg-delete-t"
    aria-describedby="dg-delete-d"
>
    <span class="bk-dialog-icon">
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            data-size="lg"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-trash" />
        </svg>
    </span>
    <div class="bk-dialog-header">
        <h2
            class="bk-dialog-title"
            id="dg-delete-t"
        >
            Delete "Lisbon, 4 nights"?
        </h2>
        <p
            class="bk-dialog-description"
            id="dg-delete-d"
        >
            The plan and notes are removed for all 6 travellers. This can't be
            undone.
        </p>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-dialog-footer">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="outline"
            type="button"
            data-bk-close
            autofocus
        >
            Keep trip
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="destructive"
            type="button"
            data-bk-close="delete"
        >
            Delete trip
        </button>
    </div>
</dialog>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Dialog, Button, Field, Input } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Edit profile</Button>
<Dialog
    open={open}
    onOpenChange={setOpen}
    title="Edit profile"
    description="Your name shows on shared trips."
    footer={
        <>
            <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
                Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button onClick={save}>Save</Button>
        </>
    }
>
    <Field label="Name">
        <Input defaultValue="Maya Kim" autoFocus />
    </Field>
</Dialog>
```

### Confirmation

```tsx
<Dialog
    variant="alert"
    icon={<Trash2 />}
    open={confirming}
    onOpenChange={setConfirming}
    title={`Delete "${trip.name}"?`}
    description="The plan and notes are removed for all travellers. This can't be undone."
    footer={
        <>
            <Button
                variant="outline"
                onClick={() => setConfirming(false)}
            >
                Keep trip
            </Button>
            <Button
                variant="destructive"
                onClick={remove}
            >
                Delete trip
            </Button>
        </>
    }
/>;
```

Alert dialogs are narrower, hide the × button and ignore backdrop clicks, so the choice is deliberate.

### HTML

Any button with `data-bk-open="id"` opens `<dialog id="id">`. `data-bk-close` inside closes it, and `data-bk-close="value"` sets the dialog's `returnValue`. Clicking the backdrop closes default dialogs.

## API

<!-- props: DialogProps -->

## Accessibility

- The native `<dialog>` traps focus, makes the page behind inert and closes with Esc. Focus returns to the button that opened it.
- `title` and `description` are wired to `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`.
- Put `autoFocus` on the first field, or on the safe button in a confirmation.

<!-- docs/components/dropdown-menu.md -->

# Dropdown menu

> A menu of actions under a button, on the native popover API, with checkbox items, shortcuts and keyboard navigation.

```html
<button
    class="bk-button"
    data-variant="outline"
    type="button"
    popovertarget="dm-account"
>
    Maya Kim
    <svg
        class="bk-icon"
        aria-hidden="true"
    >
        <use href="#i-chevron-down" />
    </svg>
</button>
<div
    class="bk-menu"
    id="dm-account"
    popover
    role="menu"
>
    <div class="bk-menu-label">My account</div>
    <button
        class="bk-menu-item"
        role="menuitem"
        type="button"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-user" />
        </svg>
        Profile
        <span class="bk-menu-shortcut">⇧⌘P</span>
    </button>
    <button
        class="bk-menu-item"
        role="menuitem"
        type="button"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-wallet" />
        </svg>
        Billing
    </button>
    <hr class="bk-menu-separator" />
    <button
        class="bk-menu-item"
        role="menuitemcheckbox"
        aria-checked="true"
        type="button"
    >
        Email updates
    </button>
    <hr class="bk-menu-separator" />
    <button
        class="bk-menu-item"
        role="menuitem"
        data-variant="destructive"
        type="button"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-logout" />
        </svg>
        Log out
    </button>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
    DropdownMenu,
    DropdownMenuItem,
    DropdownMenuCheckboxItem,
    DropdownMenuLabel,
    DropdownMenuSeparator,
    Button,
} from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<DropdownMenu
    trigger={<Button variant="outline">Maya Kim</Button>}
    align="end"
>
    <DropdownMenuLabel>My account</DropdownMenuLabel>
    <DropdownMenuItem
        icon={<User />}
        shortcut="⇧⌘P"
        onSelect={openProfile}
    >
        Profile
    </DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
        checked={emails}
        onCheckedChange={setEmails}
    >
        Email updates
    </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem
        variant="destructive"
        onSelect={logout}
    >
        Log out
    </DropdownMenuItem>
</DropdownMenu>;
```

The menu opens under its trigger, lines up with `align` (`start`, `center`, `end`) and flips above when there's no room below. Choosing an item closes it unless the item has `keepOpen`.

## API

### DropdownMenu

<!-- props: DropdownMenuProps -->

### DropdownMenuItem

<!-- props: DropdownMenuItemProps -->

### DropdownMenuCheckboxItem

<!-- props: DropdownMenuCheckboxItemProps -->

`DropdownMenuLabel` and `DropdownMenuSeparator` render a label and a divider.

## Accessibility

- Focus moves to the first item when the menu opens. ↑/↓, Home and End move between items; Esc and outside clicks close it.
- Items use `role="menuitem"` or `menuitemcheckbox` with `aria-checked`. The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="menu"`.

<!-- docs/components/popover.md -->

# Popover

> A floating panel anchored to a button, for a small form or extra details.

```html
<button
    class="bk-button"
    data-variant="outline"
    type="button"
    popovertarget="pv-invite"
>
    <svg
        class="bk-icon"
        aria-hidden="true"
    >
        <use href="#i-plus" />
    </svg>
    Invite
</button>
<div
    class="bk-popover"
    id="pv-invite"
    popover
    role="dialog"
    aria-label="Invite to trip"
>
    <div class="bk-stack">
        <div>
            <div class="bk-tile-title">Invite to trip</div>
            <p class="bk-tile-description">They can view and edit the plan.</p>
        </div>
        <input
            class="bk-input"
            type="email"
            placeholder="friend@example.com"
            aria-label="Email address"
        />
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-size="sm"
            type="button"
            popovertarget="pv-invite"
            popovertargetaction="hide"
            data-bk-toast='{"title":"Invite sent","variant":"success"}'
        >
            Send invite
        </button>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
    Popover,
    closePopover,
    Field,
    Input,
    Button,
} from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Popover
    trigger={<Button variant="outline">Invite</Button>}
    aria-label="Invite to trip"
>
    <Field label="Email">
        <Input type="email" />
    </Field>
    <Button
        size="sm"
        onClick={(e) => {
            send();
            closePopover(e);
        }}
    >
        Send invite
    </Button>
</Popover>;
```

## API

<!-- props: PopoverProps -->

`closePopover(event)` closes the popover that contains the element the event came from.

The panel grows from the trigger’s position. When placement flips above the trigger or shifts away from a viewport edge, the animation origin follows that placement. Reduced-motion preferences suppress the transition.

## Accessibility

- Esc and clicks outside close it. Focus moves to the first field when it opens.
- Give it an `aria-label` that says what the panel is for.
- For text-only hints, use a [Tooltip](tooltip.md). For a blocking choice, use a [Dialog](dialog.md).

# Sheet

> A panel that slides in from the side, or from the bottom on phones, for filters, details and share menus.

```html
<div class="bk-row">

        class="bk-button"

            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"

        class="bk-button"
        data-variant="outline"
        type="button"
        data-bk-open="sh-share"

        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-users" />

    class="bk-sheet"

            aria-hidden="true"

            class="bk-dialog-title"

        >
            Filters
        </h2>

    <div class="bk-dialog-body">
        <label class="bk-option">
            <input
                class="bk-checkbox"
                type="checkbox"
                checked
            />

        </label>

            <input
                class="bk-checkbox"
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Sheet, Button } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

    open={open}
    onOpenChange={setOpen}
    title="Filters"
    description="142 stays match."
    footer={<Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Show 142 stays</Button>}
>

</Sheet>

    side="bottom"
    open={sharing}
    onOpenChange={setSharing}
    title="Share trip"
>
    …
</Sheet>
```

## API

<!-- props: SheetProps -->

## Accessibility

- Same as [Dialog](dialog.md): focus trap, Esc to close, inert background, focus returns to the trigger.
- Bottom sheets add a drag handle for looks only. Close them with the backdrop, Esc or a button.

<!-- docs/components/bottom-nav.md -->

# Bottom nav

> A mobile tab bar for three to five primary destinations.

```html
<nav
    class="bk-bottom-nav"
    aria-label="Tabs"
    style="width: 340px"
>
    <a
        class="bk-bottom-nav-item"
        href="#"
        aria-current="page"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-home" />
        </svg>
        Home
    </a>
    <a
        class="bk-bottom-nav-item"
        href="#"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-search" />
        </svg>
        Explore
    </a>
    <a
        class="bk-bottom-nav-item"
        href="#"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-plane" />
        </svg>
        Trips
    </a>
    <a
        class="bk-bottom-nav-item"
        href="#"
    >

            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >

    </a>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { BottomNav, BottomNavItem } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<BottomNav aria-label="Tabs">
    <BottomNavItem
        href="/"
        icon={<Home />}
        current
    >
        Home
    </BottomNavItem>
    <BottomNavItem
        href="/trips"
        icon={<Plane />}
    >
        Trips
    </BottomNavItem>
</BottomNav>;
```

Fix it to the bottom of the screen in your layout, with `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` padding for phones with a home indicator.

## API

<!-- props: BottomNavItemProps -->

## Accessibility

- Every item has a visible label, not just an icon.
- The current destination has `aria-current="page"`.

<!-- docs/components/breadcrumb.md -->

# Breadcrumb

> Shows where the current page sits in the hierarchy, with links back up.

```html
<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
    <ol class="bk-breadcrumb">
        <li><a href="#">Trips</a></li>
        <li><a href="#">Lisbon</a></li>
        <li><span aria-current="page">Day 2</span></li>
    </ol>
</nav>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';
import Link from 'next/link';

<Breadcrumb
    items={[
        { label: 'Trips', href: '/trips' },
        { label: 'Lisbon', href: '/trips/lisbon' },
        { label: 'Day 2' },
    ]}
    linkAs={Link}
/>;
```

## API

<!-- props: BreadcrumbProps -->

## Accessibility

- A `nav` labelled "Breadcrumb" holding an ordered list; the last item has `aria-current="page"`.
- The separators are drawn by CSS, so screen readers don't read them.

<!-- docs/components/navbar.md -->

# Navbar

> A floating pill navigation bar with brand, links and actions. Links scroll sideways on narrow screens.

```html
<nav
    class="bk-navbar"
    aria-label="Main"
>
    <a
        class="bk-navbar-brand"
        href="#"
    >
        Tripline
    </a>
    <div class="bk-navbar-links">
        <a
            class="bk-navbar-link"
            href="#"
            aria-current="page"
        >
            Trips
        </a>
        <a
            class="bk-navbar-link"
            href="#"
        >
            Explore
        </a>
        <a
            class="bk-navbar-link"
            href="#"
        >
            Saved
        </a>
    </div>
    <div class="bk-navbar-actions">
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-variant="ghost"
            data-size="icon-sm"
            type="button"
            aria-label="Notifications"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-bell" />
            </svg>
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-button"
            data-size="sm"
            type="button"
        >
            <svg
                class="bk-icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            >
                <use href="#i-plus" />
            </svg>
            New trip
        </button>
    </div>
</nav>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
    Navbar,
    NavbarBrand,
    NavbarLinks,
    NavbarLink,
    NavbarActions,
    Button,
} from 'bento-shad-ui/react';
import Link from 'next/link';

<Navbar aria-label="Main">
    <NavbarBrand asChild>
        <Link href="/">Tripline</Link>
    </NavbarBrand>
    <NavbarLinks>
        <NavbarLink
            asChild
            current={pathname === '/trips'}
        >
            <Link href="/trips">Trips</Link>
        </NavbarLink>
        <NavbarLink
            asChild
            current={pathname === '/explore'}
        >
            <Link href="/explore">Explore</Link>
        </NavbarLink>
    </NavbarLinks>
    <NavbarActions>
        <Button size="sm">New trip</Button>
    </NavbarActions>
</Navbar>;
```

## API

### NavbarLink and NavbarBrand

<!-- props: LinkLikeProps -->

`Navbar`, `NavbarLinks` and `NavbarActions` render a `nav` and two `div`s.

## Accessibility

- Give the `nav` an `aria-label`, and mark the current page with `current` (`aria-current="page"`).
- On phones, consider moving primary destinations to a [Bottom nav](bottom-nav.md).

<!-- docs/components/pagination.md -->

# Pagination

> Move through pages of a long list, with first, last and nearby pages always visible.

```html
<nav
    class="bk-pagination"
    aria-label="Pagination"
>
    <a
        class="bk-pagination-link"
        href="#"
        aria-label="Previous page"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-chevron-left" />
        </svg>
    </a>
    <a
        class="bk-pagination-link"
        href="#"
    >
        1
    </a>
    <span
        class="bk-pagination-ellipsis"
        aria-hidden="true"
    >
        …
    </span>
    <a
        class="bk-pagination-link"
        href="#"
    >
        5
    </a>
    <a
        class="bk-pagination-link"
        href="#"
        aria-current="page"
    >
        6
    </a>
    <a
        class="bk-pagination-link"
        href="#"
    >
        7
    </a>
    <span
        class="bk-pagination-ellipsis"
        aria-hidden="true"
    >
        …
    </span>
    <a
        class="bk-pagination-link"
        href="#"
    >
        20
    </a>
    <a
        class="bk-pagination-link"
        href="#"
        aria-label="Next page"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-chevron-right" />
        </svg>
    </a>
</nav>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Pagination, getPaginationRange } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Pagination page={page} pageCount={20} onPageChange={setPage} />
// Server-rendered lists: real links
<Pagination page={page} pageCount={20} getHref={(p) => `?page=${p}`} />
getPaginationRange(6, 20); // [1, 'ellipsis', 5, 6, 7, 'ellipsis', 20]
```

## API

<!-- props: PaginationProps -->

## Accessibility

- The current page has `aria-current="page"`; each number has a label such as "Page 6".
- Previous and Next are disabled at the ends rather than hidden, so the layout doesn't shift.

<!-- docs/components/sidebar.md -->

# Sidebar

> App navigation with a brand, grouped items, counts and a footer.

```html
<nav
    class="bk-sidebar"
    aria-label="App"
    style="width: 240px"
>
    <div class="bk-sidebar-brand">Tripline</div>
    <a
        class="bk-sidebar-item"
        href="#"
        aria-current="page"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-home" />
        </svg>
        Home
    </a>
    <a
        class="bk-sidebar-item"
        href="#"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-plane" />
        </svg>
        Trips
        <span
            class="bk-badge"
            data-variant="secondary"
        >
            4
        </span>
    </a>
    <a
        class="bk-sidebar-item"
        href="#"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-inbox" />
        </svg>
        Inbox
        <span
            class="bk-badge"
            data-variant="brand"
        >
            2
        </span>
    </a>
    <div class="bk-sidebar-label">Workspace</div>
    <a
        class="bk-sidebar-item"
        href="#"
    >
        <svg
            class="bk-icon"
            aria-hidden="true"
        >
            <use href="#i-sliders" />
        </svg>
        Settings
    </a>
    <div class="bk-sidebar-footer">
        <span
            class="bk-avatar"
            data-size="sm"
            data-status="online"
        >
            MK
        </span>
        <div class="bk-list-item-text">
            <span>Maya Kim</span>
            <span>Plus plan</span>
        </div>
    </div>
</nav>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
    Sidebar,
    SidebarBrand,
    SidebarItem,
    SidebarLabel,
    SidebarFooter,
    Badge,
} from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Sidebar aria-label="App">
    <SidebarBrand>Tripline</SidebarBrand>
    <SidebarItem
        href="/"
        icon={<Home />}
        current
    >
        Home
    </SidebarItem>
    <SidebarItem
        href="/inbox"
        icon={<Inbox />}
        badge={<Badge variant="brand">2</Badge>}
    >
        Inbox
    </SidebarItem>
    <SidebarLabel>Workspace</SidebarLabel>
    <SidebarItem
        asChild
        icon={<Settings />}
    >
        <Link href="/settings">Settings</Link>
    </SidebarItem>
    <SidebarFooter>…</SidebarFooter>
</Sidebar>;
```

The sidebar uses the `--sidebar-*` tokens, so it can be themed separately from the page. In a bento layout, give it `rows` so it runs down the grid (see the dashboard recipe in [Layout](../layout.md)).

## API

<!-- props: SidebarItemProps -->

`Sidebar`, `SidebarBrand`, `SidebarLabel` and `SidebarFooter` render a `nav` and `div`s.

## Accessibility

- Label the `nav`, and mark the current page with `current`.
- Badges are read as part of the link ("Inbox 2"). Add hidden text if the number needs context ("2 unread").

<!-- docs/components/tabs.md -->

# Tabs

> Switch between views in one place. Pill and underline styles, with full keyboard support.

```html
<div
    data-bk-tabs
    style="width: 340px"
>
    <div
        class="bk-tabs-list"
        role="tablist"
        aria-label="Itinerary view"
    >
        <button
            class="bk-tabs-trigger"
            role="tab"
            type="button"
            aria-controls="tb-day"
        >
            Day
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-tabs-trigger"
            role="tab"
            type="button"
            aria-controls="tb-week"
            aria-selected="true"
        >
            Week
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-tabs-trigger"
            role="tab"
            type="button"
            aria-controls="tb-month"
        >
            Month
        </button>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-tabs-content"
        role="tabpanel"
        id="tb-day"
        hidden
    >
        <span class="bk-num">3</span>
        <span class="bk-muted">activities today</span>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-tabs-content"
        role="tabpanel"
        id="tb-week"
    >
        <span class="bk-num">7</span>
        <span class="bk-muted">activities this week</span>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-tabs-content"
        role="tabpanel"
        id="tb-month"
        hidden
    >
        <span class="bk-num">22</span>
        <span class="bk-muted">activities in March</span>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<Tabs defaultValue="week">
    <TabsList aria-label="Itinerary view">
        <TabsTrigger value="day">Day</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="week">Week</TabsTrigger>
    </TabsList>
    <TabsContent value="day">…</TabsContent>
    <TabsContent value="week">…</TabsContent>
</Tabs>;
```

## Examples

### Underline style

```html
<div
    data-bk-tabs
    style="width: 340px"
>
    <div
        class="bk-tabs-list"
        data-variant="line"
        role="tablist"
        aria-label="Trip sections"
    >
        <button
            class="bk-tabs-trigger"
            role="tab"
            type="button"
            aria-controls="tl-a"
            aria-selected="true"
        >
            Itinerary
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-tabs-trigger"
            role="tab"
            type="button"
            aria-controls="tl-b"
        >
            Bookings
        </button>
        <button
            class="bk-tabs-trigger"
            role="tab"
            type="button"
            aria-controls="tl-c"
        >
            Notes
        </button>
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-tabs-content bk-muted"
        role="tabpanel"
        id="tl-a"
    >
        4 days, 11 stops.
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-tabs-content bk-muted"
        role="tabpanel"
        id="tl-b"
        hidden
    >
        2 flights, 1 hotel.
    </div>
    <div
        class="bk-tabs-content bk-muted"
        role="tabpanel"
        id="tl-c"
        hidden
    >
        3 notes from 2 people.
    </div>
</div>
```

```tsx

<TabsList variant="line">…</TabsList>
<TabsList full>…</TabsList> {/* triggers fill the width */}
```

## API

### Tabs

<!-- props: TabsProps -->

### TabsList

<!-- props: TabsListProps -->

### TabsTrigger

<!-- props: TabsTriggerProps -->

### TabsContent

<!-- props: TabsContentProps -->

### HTML

Wrap the list and panels in `[data-bk-tabs]`. Each `role="tab"` button points at its panel with `aria-controls`; the script handles selection and keys.

## Accessibility

- ←/→ move between tabs and select them, Home and End jump to the ends. Only the selected tab is in the Tab order.
- Tabs and panels are linked with `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby`.

<!-- docs/components/characters.md -->

# Characters

> Eight hand-drawn pencil characters, four people and four animals, each with six moods. Use them for empty states, errors, loading, success and onboarding.

<!-- character-gallery -->

Pick a mood on any card to see it. Every character is drawn by the same pencil kit: graphite lines drawn twice and slightly wobbled, hatching for shadows, and coloured-pencil fills taken from the tint tokens. Lines follow the text colour, so in dark mode they turn into chalk on dark paper.

## Usage

```tsx
import { PencilCharacter, Empty, Button } from 'bento-shad-ui/react';

<PencilCharacter character="pip" mood="thinking" size={160} />

<Empty
    illustration={<PencilCharacter character="pip" mood="thinking" />}
    title="No trips yet"
    description="Trips you plan or get invited to show up here."
    actions={<Button>Plan a trip</Button>}
/>
```

In HTML, load the illustrations script once. It draws every element with `data-bk-character`, including ones added later, and redraws when `data-mood` changes:

```html
<script
    src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/illustrations.iife.min.js"
    defer
></script>

<span
    data-bk-character="moss"
    data-mood="sleepy"
    data-size="140"
    aria-label="Moss the turtle, waiting"
></span>
```

```js
document.querySelector('[data-bk-character]').dataset.mood = 'happy'; // redraws
```

Or use a ready-made file. These use plain colours instead of tokens, so they work in `<img>`, email, Figma and Flutter:

```html
<img
    src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bento-shad-ui@0.2.2/dist/illustrations/biscuit-surprised.svg"
    width="160"
    height="160"
    alt=""
/>
```

Files are named `<character>-<mood>.svg`, for example `pip-thinking.svg`. `dist/illustrations/index.json` lists all of them.

### Any JavaScript

```ts
import {
    renderCharacter,
    characters,
    moods,
} from 'bento-shad-ui/illustrations';

el.innerHTML = renderCharacter('dumpling', 'sad', {
    title: 'Dumpling the cat, looking sorry',
});
characters.map((c) => c.name); // ['Mira', 'Theo', 'Zara', 'Kofi', 'Pip', 'Dumpling', 'Biscuit', 'Moss']
```

`renderCharacter` is a pure function that returns an SVG string, so it also works on the server and in build scripts. Pass a unique `idPrefix` when you render the same character more than once on a page.

### Flutter

Copy the SVG files into `assets/characters/` and draw them with `flutter_svg`. The pencil uses `currentColor`, so `SvgTheme` sets it:

```dart
SvgPicture.asset(
  'assets/characters/pip-thinking.svg',
  width: 160,
  theme: SvgTheme(currentColor: Theme.of(context).extension<BentoColors>()!.foreground),
)
```

## Which character for which moment

| Situation | Character and mood |
|---|---|
| Empty list, no search results | Pip, `thinking` |
| Loading, waiting, slow connection | Moss, `sleepy` |
| Success, booking confirmed | Mira, `happy` |
| Error, failed action | Dumpling, `sad` |
| Page not found | Biscuit, `surprised` |
| Offline, no messages | Zara, `sad` |
| Welcome, guided tour, tips | Theo, `neutral` or `happy` |
| Achievement, first trip planned | Kofi, `happy` |

## Moods

| Mood | Face | Extra |
|---|---|---|
| `neutral` | Open eyes, soft smile | Light blush |
| `happy` | Closed smiling eyes, open smile | Blush |
| `surprised` | Wide eyes, raised brows, round mouth | Motion lines |
| `sad` | Drooping brows, frown | A tear |
| `thinking` | Eyes looking up, one brow raised | Thought bubble with "?" |
| `sleepy` | Closed eyes, small mouth | "z z" |

## Changing the pencil colour

The graphite colour is `--pencil`, which defaults to a mix of `--foreground` and `--background`. Override it on any parent:

```css
.onboarding {
    --pencil: var(--brand);
}
```

## API

<!-- props: PencilCharacterProps -->

## Accessibility

- Characters are decorative by default: the SVG is hidden from screen readers. Pass `label` (React) or `aria-label` (HTML) only when the drawing adds meaning the text around it doesn't already give.
- Never put information only in the drawing. An empty state still needs its title and description.
- The drawings have no animation, so they're unaffected by reduced-motion settings.
